{"path": "/app/ars.R", "content": "## =============================================================================
##  ars.R  --  Adaptive Rejection Sampling (ARS)
##
##  Implementation of the adaptive rejection sampler of
##      Gilks, W. R. & Wild, P. (1992). Adaptive rejection sampling for Gibbs
##      sampling. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C (Applied
##      Statistics), 41(2), 337-348.
##
##  The sampler targets an arbitrary *log-concave* (possibly unnormalised)
##  density on an interval of the real line.  It works entirely with the
##  log-density h(x) = log f(x) and maintains a piecewise-linear envelope
##  (upper hull) built from the tangents of h at the abscissae of an
##  "abscissae set" T_k, together with a piecewise-exponential squeezing
##  function (lower hull) built from the chords between consecutive abscissae.
##  Points are proposed from the envelope and are accepted with probability
##  exp(h - envelope); whenever the squeeze test fails and the point is not
##  accepted it is added to T_k, sharpening both hulls.
##
##  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
##  File layout (modular design)
##  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
##   1. Input validation helpers      (very small, focused checks)
##   2. Log-density / derivative     (numerical derivatives, normalisation)
##   3. Abscissae-set management     (insertion, sorting, domain search)
##   4. Hull construction            (envelope + squeeze: piecewise exp form)
##   5. Envelope / squeeze evaluation and sampling from the envelope
##   6. Core (vectorised) sampling loop  + log-concavity checks
##   7. User-facing `ars()`          (validation, dispatch, diagnostics)
##   8. Testing framework: `test()`  (formal tests against known truth)
##
##  Naming conventions
##  ---------------
##  * internal helpers are prefixed `ars_` and use lower_snake_case verbs
##      ars_validate_*   : input validation
##  * hull objects are plain lists with a well-defined, documented structure
##      list(intercepts = numeric(m+2), slopes = numeric(m+2))
##    (intercepts/slopes are *per-line* coefficients; see `ars_build_hull`)
##  * everything returns plain R objects (no S3 classes are required by callers)
## =============================================================================


## =============================================================================
## 1. INPUT VALIDATION HELPERS
## =============================================================================

## Throw a uniform, informative error.
ars_stop <- function(...) {
  stop(paste0(...), call. = FALSE)
}

## Is `x` a single, finite, non-NA numeric value?
ars_is_number <- function(x) {
  is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1L && !is.na(x) && is.finite(x)
}

## Validate the target: an R function that is vectorised in its first argument.
ars_validate_fun <- function(fun) {
  if (missing(fun) || is.null(fun))
    ars_stop("`fun` must be supplied: a (vectorised) function evaluating the ",
             "unnormalised density of the target distribution.")
  if (!is.function(fun))
    ars_stop("`fun` must be a function (e.g. `dnorm`, `dexp` or `function(x) ...`); ",
             "got an object of class '", paste(class(fun), collapse = "/"), "'.")

  ## Probe the function once to make sure it is vectorised and usable.
  probe <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(fun(c(-1.2345, 0, 0.6789))),
    error = function(e) ars_stop("`fun` could not be evaluated on a numeric vector: ",
                                 conditionMessage(e))
  )
  if (!is.numeric(probe))
    ars_stop("`fun` must return a numeric vector; it returned class '",
             paste(class(probe), collapse = "/"), "'.")
  if (length(probe) != 3L)
    ars_stop("`fun` must be vectorised: evaluating it on 3 inputs returned ",
             length(probe), " value(s). Use e.g. `function(x) dnorm(x, log = FALSE)` ",
             "or a call wrapped in Vectorize().")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

## Validate a single sample size.
ars_validate_n <- function(n) {
  if (!is.numeric(n) || length(n) != 1L || is.na(n))
    ars_stop("`n` must be a single non-missing number.")
  if (!is.finite(n))
    ars_stop("`n` must be finite; got ", n, ".")
  if (n < 1)
    ars_stop("`n` must be a positive integer (number of samples); got ", n, ".")
  if (n != as.integer(n))
    ars_stop("`n` must be a whole number; got ", format(n), ".")
  if (n > 1e8)
    ars_stop("`n` is unreasonably large (> 1e8); refusing to allocate.")
  as.integer(n)
}

## Validate the (lower, upper) domain.  `-Inf`/`Inf` are allowed (and are the
## natural choice for unbounded support); at least one bound must be finite so
## that the initial abscissae can be found.
ars_validate_domain <- function(lower, upper) {
  if (!ars_is_number(lower))
    ars_stop("`lower` must be a single finite number (use -Inf for an unbounded ",
             "left support but give a finite starting point when derivative = NULL).")
  if (!ars_is_number(upper))
    ars_stop("`upper` must be a single finite number (use Inf for an unbounded ",
             "right support but give a finite starting point when derivative = NULL).")
  ## -Inf/Inf themselves are *not* numbers by `ars_is_number`, so re-allow them:
  ok_lower <- is.numeric(lower) && length(lower) == 1L && !is.na(lower)
  ok_upper <- is.numeric(upper) && length(upper) == 1L && !is.na(upper)
  if (!ok_lower || !ok_upper)
    ars_stop("`lower` and `upper` must each be a single number (finite, or +/-Inf).")
  if (lower >= upper)
    ars_stop("`lower` (", lower, ") must be strictly less than `upper` (", upper, ").")
  if (!is.finite(lower) && !is.finite(upper))
    ars_stop("At least one of `lower`/`upper` must be finite so that the ",
             "initial abscissae can be located.")
  c(lower = as.numeric(lower), upper = as.numeric(upper))
}

## Validate user-supplied starting abscissae.
ars_validate_x0 <- function(x0, lower, upper, fun_log) {
  if (is.null(x0)) return(NULL)
  if (!is.numeric(x0) || length(x0) < 1L)
    ars_stop("`x0` must be a numeric vector of at least one starting abscissa.")
  if (anyNA(x0) || any(!is.finite(x0)))
    ars_stop("`x0` must contain only finite numbers.")
  x0 <- sort(unique(as.numeric(x0)))
  if (any(x0 <= lower) || any(x0 >= upper))
    ars_stop("All starting abscissae `x0` must lie strictly inside ",
             "(`lower`, `upper`) = (", lower, ", ", upper, ").")
  hv <- fun_log(x0)
  bad <- !is.finite(hv)
  if (any(bad))
    ars_stop("The log-density is not finite at starting abscissa(e): ",
             paste(signif(x0[bad], 6), collapse = ", "),
             ". These points are outside the support of the target.")
  x0
}

## Validate a user-supplied derivative function.  It must be vectorised and
## produce one finite number per input.
ars_validate_deriv <- function(deriv, fun_log, x0) {
  if (is.null(deriv)) return(NULL)
  if (!is.function(deriv))
    ars_stop("`derivative` must be NULL or a (vectorised) function.")
  probe <- tryCatch(deriv(x0), error = function(e)
    ars_stop("`derivative` could not be evaluated: ", conditionMessage(e)))
  if (!is.numeric(probe) || length(probe) != length(x0))
    ars_stop("`derivative` must be vectorised and return one value per input ",
             "(got ", length(probe), " value(s) for ", length(x0), " input(s)).")
  if (any(!is.finite(probe)))
    ars_stop("`derivative` returned non-finite value(s) at the starting abscissae.")
  deriv
}

## Validate the initial abscissae / search step / search limit.
ars_validate_init <- function(x0, step, max_search) {
  if (!ars_is_number(step) || step <= 0)
    ars_stop("`x0_step` must be a single positive number; got ",
             paste(format(step), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!ars_is_number(max_search) || max_search < 1 || max_search != as.integer(max_search))
    ars_stop("`max_search` must be a positive integer; got ",
             paste(format(max_search), collapse = ","), ".")
  list(step = as.numeric(step), max_search = as.integer(max_search))
}

## Validate the miscellaneous numeric / logical options.
ars_validate_opts <- function(n_env, max_iter, tol, concavity_tol, verbose) {
  if (!ars_is_number(n_env) || n_env < 3 || n_env != as.integer(n_env))
    ars_stop("`n_env` (initial abscissae count) must be an integer >= 3; got ",
             paste(format(n_env), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!ars_is_number(max_iter) || max_iter < 1 || max_iter != as.integer(max_iter))
    ars_stop("`max_iter` must be a positive integer; got ",
             paste(format(max_iter), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!ars_is_number(tol) || tol < 0)
    ars_stop("`tol` (derivative tolerance for log-concavity checks) must be a ",
             "non-negative number; got ", paste(format(tol), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!ars_is_number(concavity_tol) || concavity_tol < 0)
    ars_stop("`concavity_tol` must be a non-negative number; got ",
             paste(format(concavity_tol), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!is.logical(verbose) || length(verbose) != 1L || is.na(verbose))
    ars_stop("`verbose` must be TRUE or FALSE.")
  list(n_env = as.integer(n_env), max_iter = as.integer(max_iter),
       tol = as.numeric(tol), concavity_tol = as.numeric(concavity_tol),
       verbose = verbose)
}


## =============================================================================
## 2. LOG-DENSITY AND DERIVATIVE
## =============================================================================

## Build the log-density function h(x) = log f(x) from the user's density.
##   * `log_fun = TRUE`  : `fun` already returns log f.
##   * `log_fun = FALSE` : `fun` returns f, and we take logs here.
## Non-finite results are allowed (they signal "outside the support"), but
## NaN and positive infinities are turned into -Inf / +Inf explicitly so that
## later arithmetic behaves predictably.
ars_make_log_density <- function(fun, log_fun) {
  force(fun); force(log_fun)
  function(x) {
    v <- fun(x)
    h <- if (log_fun) v else log(v)
    h[is.nan(h)] <- -Inf
    h
  }
}

## Numerically differentiate the log-density at a single point using a
## central difference (with an automatic step that respects the scale of `x`).
## The result is *checked for log-concavity consistency* by the caller.
ars_num_deriv1 <- function(fun_log, x, lower, upper) {
  h <- fun_log(x)
  if (!is.finite(h))
    ars_stop("Cannot differentiate the log-density at x = ", signif(x, 8),
             ": log-density is not finite there.")
  ## step size: scaled, and kept strictly inside the domain when possible
  dx <- 1e-5 * max(1, abs(x))
  xl <- x - dx; xr <- x + dx
  if (is.finite(lower) && xl <= lower) { xl <- x; dx <- (xr - x) }
  if (is.finite(upper) && xr >= upper) { xr <- x; dx <- (x - xl) }
  if (!is.finite(lower) && !is.finite(upper)) { xl <- x - dx; xr <- x + dx }
  hl <- fun_log(xl); hr <- fun_log(xr)
  if (!is.finite(hl) || !is.finite(hr))
    ars_stop("Numerical differentiation of the log-density failed near x = ",
             signif(x, 8), " (log-density not finite on a neighbourhood).")
  (hr - hl) / (xr - xl)
}

## Return a vectorised derivative function of x.
## If the user supplies `derivative`, it is used directly.  Otherwise a
## numerical derivative is built by calling `ars_num_deriv1` element-wise.
ars_make_derivative <- function(deriv, fun_log, lower, upper) {
  if (!is.null(deriv)) {
    force(deriv)
    return(function(x) as.numeric(deriv(x)))
  }
  force(fun_log); force(lower); force(upper)
  function(x) vapply(as.numeric(x), function(xi)
    ars_num_deriv1(fun_log, xi, lower, upper), numeric(1))
}


## =============================================================================
## 3. ABSCISSAE-SET MANAGEMENT
## =============================================================================

## Insert `x_new` into the sorted abscissae vector `Tk`, keeping it sorted and
## unique.  Returns the new vector.
ars_insert_abscissa <- function(Tk, x_new, tol = 1e-12) {
  if (any(abs(Tk - x_new) <= tol * max(1, abs(x_new)))) return(Tk)  # already there
  sort(c(Tk, x_new))
}

## Compute log-density and (first) derivative at every abscissa of `Tk`.
## Returns list(x = Tk, h = h(Tk), dh = h'(Tk)).
ars_eval_abscissae <- function(Tk, fun_log, fun_deriv, tol) {
  h  <- fun_log(Tk)
  if (any(!is.finite(h)))
    ars_stop("The log-density is not finite at abscissa(e) ",
             paste(signif(Tk[!is.finite(h)], 6), collapse = ", "),
             ". Those points lie outside the support of the target; supply ",
             "starting abscissae `x0` inside the support.")
  dh <- fun_deriv(Tk)
  ## log-concavity check #1: slope of the tangent must be (numerically) 
  ## non-increasing over the abscissae.
  if (length(dh) > 1L) {
    dif <- diff(dh)
    if (any(dif > tol))
      ars_stop("Density is not log-concave: the derivative of the log-density ",
               "increases between abscissae ",
               paste(signif(Tk[which(dif > tol)], 6), "->",
                     signif(Tk[which(dif > tol) + 1L], 6), collapse = ", "),
               " (increase = ", signif(max(dif), 4), " > tol = ", tol, "). ",
               "ARS requires a log-concave target.")
  }
  list(x = Tk, h = h, dh = dh)
}

## Locate an initial abscissae set.
##
## Strategy:
##   * If `x0` is supplied it is used (validated inside the domain).
##     Additional points are added by growing a grid around it if fewer than
##     `n_env` points are available.
##   * Otherwise a symmetric grid (or a one-sided grid, when the domain is
##     one-sided) of `n_env` points is laid out inside the domain and then
##     filtered to points where the log-density is finite.
## The result always contains at least two points with finite log-density.
ars_find_abscissae <- function(fun_log, lower, upper, x0, n_env, step, max_search) {
  finite_domain <- is.finite(lower) && is.finite(upper)

  if (!is.null(x0)) {
    Tk <- x0
  } else if (finite_domain) {
    Tk <- seq(lower + (upper - lower) / (n_env + 1),
              upper - (upper - lower) / (n_env + 1),
              length.out = n_env)
  } else {
    ## One-sided (or `-Inf`/`Inf`) domains: start from a unit-scale grid and
    ## expand until `n_env` finite-h points are found.
    centre <- if (is.finite(lower)) lower + 1 else upper - 1
    Tk <- centre + step * 0  # placeholder; populated below
    cand <- centre + step * (0:(max_search - 1))
    cand <- cand[cand > lower & cand < upper]
    hh <- fun_log(cand)
    cand <- cand[is.finite(hh)]
    if (length(cand) < 2L)
      ars_stop("Could not find two abscissae with finite log-density near ",
               signif(centre, 6), "; please supply `x0`.")
    Tk <- cand[seq_len(min(n_env, length(cand)))]
  }

  ## Clean up: keep points strictly inside the domain with finite log-density.
  Tk <- sort(unique(as.numeric(Tk)))
  Tk <- Tk[Tk > lower & Tk < upper]
  hh <- fun_log(Tk)
  Tk <- Tk[is.finite(hh)]

  ## Grow the set (outwards, on a geometric ladder) until it is large enough.
  if (length(Tk) < max(2L, n_env)) {
    grow <- function(side) {
      last <- if (side == "right") max(Tk) else min(Tk)
      for (k in seq_len(max_search)) {
        cand <- last + (if (side == "right") 1 else -1) * step * 2^(k - 1)
        if (cand <= lower || cand >= upper) break
        hv <- fun_log(cand)
        if (is.finite(hv)) { Tk <<- sort(unique(c(Tk, cand))); last <- cand }
        if (length(Tk) >= n_env) break
      }
    }
    grow("right")
    if (length(Tk) < n_env) grow("left")
  }

  if (length(Tk) < 2L)
    ars_stop("Unable to locate at least two abscissae with finite log-density ",
             "inside (", lower, ", ", upper, "). Check the domain and the ",
             "support of the target, or pass `x0`.")
  Tk
}

## Derive the effective support from the domain and the log-density.
## A finite `lower`/`upper` is moved to the boundary of the support if the
## log-density is -Inf at the boundary itself but finite just inside it.
ars_effective_domain <- function(fun_log, lower, upper, step) {
  eps <- step * 1e-6
  if (is.finite(lower) && !is.finite(fun_log(lower)) && is.finite(fun_log(lower + eps)))
    lower <- lower
  invisible(c(lower, upper))
}


## =============================================================================
## 4. HULL CONSTRUCTION
## =============================================================================
##
## With abscissae x_1 < ... < x_k and tangents l_i(x) = h_i + h'_i (x - x_i),
##
##   upper hull  u_k(x) = min_{i <= k in (z_{i-1}, z_i)} l_i(x)
##   lower hull  L_k(x) = chord between (x_i, h_i) and (x_{i+1}, h_{i+1})
##                        on (x_i, x_{i+1}),
##
## where z_0 = lower, z_k = upper and z_i (i = 1..k-1) is the intersection
## point of tangents l_i and l_{i+1}:
##      z_i = (h_{i+1} - h_i - h'_{i+1} x_{i+1} + h'_i x_i) / (h'_i - h'_{i+1}).
##
## Each piece of *both* hulls is an exponential of a straight line
##   exp(a + b x),
## so the pieces are stored as `intercepts` (a) and `slopes` (b) vectors with
## one entry per interval:
##   interval 1      : (-Inf, z_1)                -> tangent at x_1
##   interval i (2..k-1): (z_{i-1}, z_i)          -> tangent at x_i,  chord (i-1,i)
##   interval k      : (z_{k-1}, +Inf)            -> tangent at x_k,  chord (k-1,k)
## The outer intervals are truncated at `lower`/`upper` when those are finite.

## Compute the intersection abscissae z_1, ..., z_{k-1} of consecutive tangents.
ars_intersections <- function(x, h, dh) {
  k <- length(x)
  if (k < 2L) return(numeric(0))
  i <- seq_len(k - 1L)
  denom <- dh[i] - dh[i + 1L]
  z <- (h[i + 1L] - h[i] - dh[i + 1L] * x[i + 1L] + dh[i] * x[i]) / denom
  ## Guard: if two tangents are (numerically) parallel the intersection is
  ## undefined.  Fall back to the mid-point, which is the correct limit for a
  ## piecewise-linear (zero-curvature) region.
  bad <- !is.finite(z)
  if (any(bad)) z[bad] <- (x[i][bad] + x[i + 1L][bad]) / 2
  z
}

## Build the upper (envelope) and lower (squeeze) hulls from an abscissae set.
## Returns list(env = hull, squeeze = hull, z = intersections, lower, upper)
ars_build_hull <- function(x, h, dh, lower, upper) {
  k <- length(x)
  z <- ars_intersections(x, h, dh)

  ## --- upper hull: tangent lines, one per interval -------------------------
  ## tangent at x_i:  a_i + b_i * x  with b_i = dh_i, a_i = h_i - dh_i x_i
  a_tan <- h - dh * x
  b_tan <- dh

  ## --- lower hull: chord between consecutive abscissae ---------------------
  ## chord on (x_i, x_{i+1}): slope (h_{i+1}-h_i)/(x_{i+1}-x_i), intercept below
  if (k >= 2L) {
    dx <- diff(x)
    s  <- diff(h) / dx
    a_chord <- h[-k] - s * x[-k]
  } else {
    s <- numeric(0); a_chord <- numeric(0)
  }

  ## interval boundaries
  env_bounds     <- c(lower, z, upper)
  squeeze_bounds <- c(lower, x, upper)

  list(
    env     = list(intercepts = a_tan, slopes = b_tan, bounds = env_bounds),
    squeeze = list(intercepts = a_chord, slopes = s, bounds = squeeze_bounds),
    z = z, x = x, h = h, dh = dh, lower = lower, upper = upper
  )
}

## Log of the envelope evaluated on the grid of interval boundaries (used for
## the sampled-probability mass of each interval, and for normalisation).
## For each interval j with bounds (lo_j, hi_j) and line (a_j, b_j), the
## integral of exp(a + b x) over [lo, hi] is computed in closed form.
ars_piece_logmass <- function(hull) {
  a <- hull$intercepts; b <- hull$slopes; bd <- hull$bounds
  lo <- bd[-length(bd)]; hi <- bd[-1]
  ## antiderivative: exp(a + b x)/b  (b != 0)  or  exp(a) * x  (b == 0)
  anti <- function(x) {
    out <- numeric(length(x))
    nz <- b != 0
    out[nz]  <- exp(a[nz] + b[nz] * x[nz]) / b[nz]
    out[!nz] <- exp(a[!nz]) * x[!nz]
    out
  }
  logmass <- log(pmax(anti(hi) - anti(lo), .Machine$double.xmin))
  logmass
}


## =============================================================================
## 5. ENVELOPE / SQUEEZE EVALUATION AND ENVELOPE SAMPLING
## =============================================================================

## Evaluate the piecewise-exponential hull at arbitrary `x`.
##   hull: list(intercepts, slopes, bounds)
## Returns a numeric vector, one value per `x` ( -Inf outside the bounds ).
ars_eval_hull <- function(x, hull) {
  a <- hull$intercepts; b <- hull$slopes; bd <- hull$bounds
  idx <- findInterval(x, bd, rightmost.closed = TRUE, all.inside = FALSE)
  out <- rep(-Inf, length(x))
  inside <- idx >= 1L & idx <= length(a)
  if (any(inside)) {
    ii <- idx[inside]
    out[inside] <- a[ii] + b[ii] * x[inside]
  }
  out
}

## Return the interval index (1..m) containing each `x`, 0 when outside.
ars_interval_index <- function(x, bounds) {
  idx <- findInterval(x, bounds, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
  idx[idx < 1L | idx > length(bounds) - 1L] <- 0L
  idx
}

## Sample `m` points from the piecewise-exponential envelope.
##
## Method: choose an interval with probability proportional to its probability
## mass under the envelope, then draw from the (truncated) exponential on that
## interval using inverse-cdf sampling.  This is exact and vectorised.
ars_sample_env <- function(hull, m) {
  a <- hull$intercepts; b <- hull$slopes; bd <- hull$bounds
  logmass <- ars_piece_logmass(hull)
  j <- sample.int(length(logmass), size = m, replace = TRUE, prob = exp(logmass - max(logmass)))
  lo <- bd[j]; hi <- bd[j + 1L]
  aa <- a[j]; bb <- b[j]

  u <- stats::runif(m)
  x <- numeric(m)
  nz <- bb != 0
  ## exponential: F(x) = (exp(b*x) - exp(b*lo)) / (exp(b*hi) - exp(b*lo))
  x[nz] <- log(exp(bb[nz] * lo[nz]) + u[nz] *
                (exp(bb[nz] * hi[nz]) - exp(bb[nz] * lo[nz]))) / bb[nz]
  ## flat piece (b == 0): uniform on the interval
  x[!nz] <- lo[!nz] + u[!nz] * (hi[!nz] - lo[!nz])
  ## guard against round-off at the boundaries
  x <- pmin(pmax(x, pmin(lo, hi)), pmax(lo, hi))
  x
}


## =============================================================================
## 6. CORE SAMPLING LOOP
## =============================================================================

## Log-concavity check #2: verify that the "squeeze" lies below the
## log-density at an abscissa set, and that the envelope lies above it.
## Using the fact that h is concave, testing on a dense grid of the support
## is sufficient in practice.  (Called once after warm-up.)
ars_check_logconcavity <- function(fun_log, hull, lower, upper, concavity_tol) {
  ## Choose a grid: interval boundaries plus points inside each interval.
  bd <- hull$env$bounds
  bd <- bd[is.finite(bd)]
  if (length(bd) < 2L) return(invisible(TRUE))
  grid <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(length(bd) - 1L), function(i) {
    seq(bd[i], bd[i + 1L], length.out = 5L)
  }))
  grid <- unique(grid[grid > lower & grid < upper])
  h <- fun_log(grid)
  e <- ars_eval_hull(grid, hull$env)
  ## envelope violation: h > u  (by more than the tolerance)
  viol <- which(is.finite(h) & is.finite(e) & (h > e + concavity_tol))
  if (length(viol) > 0L)
    ars_stop("Density is not log-concave: the log-density exceeds its tangent ",
             "envelope at x = ", paste(signif(grid[viol][1:min(3, length(viol))], 6),
                                       collapse = ", "),
             " (excess = ", signif(max(h[viol] - e[viol]), 4), " > ",
             "concavity_tol = ", concavity_tol, "). ARS requires a log-concave target.")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

## The core sampler.
## Iteratively proposes from the envelope, accepts with probability
## exp(h - env), and otherwise updates the abscissae set.  Uses the squeeze to
## short-circuit the acceptance step when possible.  Every time the abscissae
## set is updated we re-check log-concavity (derivative monotonicity); the
## squeeze-based check is applied at the end.
ars_sample_core <- function(fun_log, fun_deriv, n, lower, upper, Tk,
                            max_iter, tol, concavity_tol, verbose) {
  k <- length(Tk)
  if (k < 2L) ars_stop("Internal error: need >= 2 abscissae to start the sampler.")

  ## initial evaluation + log-concavity check #1
  info <- ars_eval_abscissae(Tk, fun_log, fun_deriv, tol)
  Tk <- info$x; h <- info$h; dh <- info$dh
  hull <- ars_build_hull(Tk, h, dh, lower, upper)

  ## log-concavity check #2 on the initial envelope
  ars_check_logconcavity(fun_log, hull, lower, upper, concavity_tol)

  samples <- numeric(n)
  n_done  <- 0L
  n_prop  <- 0L
  n_acc   <- 0L
  n_squeeze <- 0L
  it <- 0L
  max_total <- max_iter
  if (max_total < 10L * n) max_total <- as.integer(10L * n)  # generous safety net

  while (n_done < n) {
    it <- it + 1L
    if (it > max_total)
      ars_stop("Sampler failed to draw ", n, " accepted samples within ",
               max_total, " iterations (drawn = ", n_done, ", accepted = ",
               n_acc, "). The density may be only weakly log-concave or ",
               "mis-specified; consider supplying `x0`, `derivative`, or ",
               "increasing `max_iter`.")

    x_new  <- ars_sample_env(hull, 1L)
    n_prop <- n_prop + 1L
    h_new  <- fun_log(x_new)

    ## --- squeeze test (cheap) ------------------------------------------------
    ## lower hull at x_new; if log(u) <= squeeze - env we accept immediately.
    lq <- ars_eval_hull(x_new, hull$squeeze)
    en <- ars_eval_hull(x_new, hull$env)
    log_u <- log(stats::runif(1L))

    if (is.finite(lq) && log_u <= lq - en) {
      ## accept without evaluating the density ratio (squeeze accepted)
      n_acc <- n_acc + 1L
      n_squeeze <- n_squeeze + 1L
      n_done <- n_done + 1L
      samples[n_done] <- x_new
      next
    }

    ## --- full acceptance test ------------------------------------------------
    ok_eval <- is.finite(h_new) || (h_new == -Inf)
    if (ok_eval && log_u <= (h_new - en)) {
      n_acc <- n_acc + 1L
      n_done <- n_done + 1L
      samples[n_done] <- x_new
      ## optionally update the hull when the new point is a genuine squeeze
      ## improvement.  Here we follow Gilks & Wild: the point is accepted and
      ## *not* added (it satisfies the squeeze, so it adds no information to
      ## the lower hull).  We still add it when it is a new local maximum of
      ## information, i.e. well inside an interval (cheap improvement).
      ## -> keep it simple and faithful: do NOT update here.
      next
    }

    ## --- reject and adapt ----------------------------------------------------
    ## x_new is added to the abscissae set, provided it carries new information
    ## (not numerically coincident with an existing abscissa, and finite).
    if (!is.finite(h_new)) {
      ## outside the support -> reject, do not adapt (nothing to learn)
      next
    }
    new_Tk <- ars_insert_abscissa(Tk, x_new, tol = 1e-10)
    if (length(new_Tk) == length(Tk)) next  # coincident with an existing point

    Tk <- new_Tk
    info <- ars_eval_abscissae(Tk, fun_log, fun_deriv, tol)  # includes check #1
    h <- info$h; dh <- info$dh
    hull <- ars_build_hull(Tk, h, dh, lower, upper)
    ## recompute envelope at the rejected point for the next iteration; also
    ## re-verify the envelope lies above the log-density (check #2)
    if (it %% 5L == 0L)
      ars_check_logconcavity(fun_log, hull, lower, upper, concavity_tol)

    if (verbose && it %% 500L == 0L)
      message(sprintf("  [ars] it=%d drawn=%d accepted=%d |T|=%d",
                      it, n_done, n_acc, length(Tk)))
  }

  list(samples = samples, n_prop = n_prop, n_acc = n_acc,
       n_squeeze = n_squeeze, n_abscissae = length(Tk),
       abscissae = Tk)
}


## =============================================================================
## 7. USER-FACING `ars()`
## =============================================================================

#' Adaptive Rejection Sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992)
#'
#' Draw `n` independent samples from a target density f that is known up to a
#' normalising constant and is log-concave on its support.
#'
#' @param fun      (Vectorised) function computing the unnormalised density f.
#'                 Set `log_fun = TRUE` if it returns log f instead.
#' @param n        Number of samples to draw (positive integer).
#' @param lower,upper  Support of the target.  `-Inf`/`Inf` are allowed; at
#'                 least one bound must be finite when `x0` is not supplied.
#' @param x0       Optional numeric vector of starting abscissae (strictly
#'                 inside (lower, upper), finite log-density required).
#' @param derivative Optional vectorised function for d/dx log f.  If NULL a
#'                 numerical derivative is used.
#' @param log_fun  Logical: does `fun` return the log-density? (default FALSE)
#' @param n_env    Number of initial abscissae used to build the first envelope.
#' @param x0_step  Scale used when searching for initial abscissae / limits.
#' @param max_search  Max number of steps in that search.
#' @param max_iter Safety limit on the number of proposals.
#' @param tol      Derivative tolerance for the log-concavity check.
#' @param concavity_tol Tolerance for the envelope/squeeze concavity check.
#' @param seed     Optional integer seed (for reproducibility).
#' @param verbose  Logical: print progress?
#' @return A numeric vector of `n` samples (with attributes describing the run).
#' @export
ars <- function(fun,
                n,
                lower = -Inf,
                upper = Inf,
                x0 = NULL,
                derivative = NULL,
                log_fun = FALSE,
                n_env = 10L,
                x0_step = 1,
                max_search = 50L,
                max_iter = 100000L,
                tol = 1e-6,
                concavity_tol = 1e-6,
                seed = NULL,
                verbose = FALSE) {

  ## --- validation (fail fast, with informative messages) --------------------
  ars_validate_fun(fun)
  n   <- ars_validate_n(n)
  dom <- ars_validate_domain(lower, upper)
  lower <- dom[["lower"]]; upper <- dom[["upper"]]
  if (!is.logical(log_fun) || length(log_fun) != 1L || is.na(log_fun))
    ars_stop("`log_fun` must be TRUE or FALSE.")
  opts <- ars_validate_opts(n_env, max_iter, tol, concavity_tol, verbose)

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    if (!is.numeric(seed) || length(seed) != 1L || is.na(seed))
      ars_stop("`seed` must be NULL or a single number.")
    set.seed(as.integer(seed))
  }

  ## --- build h(x) and h'(x) --------------------------------------------------
  fun_log   <- ars_make_log_density(fun, log_fun)
  step_opts <- ars_validate_init(x0, x0_step, max_search)

  ## effective domain / support handling:
  ## when `lower`/`upper` are finite but the density is 0 there, treat them
  ## as-is (the sampler simply never proposes there because the envelope is
  ## truncated).  A user-supplied `x0` must be inside.
  if (!is.null(x0)) {
    x0 <- ars_validate_x0(x0, lower, upper, fun_log)
  }

  ## initial abscissae
  Tk <- ars_find_abscissae(fun_log, lower, upper, x0,
                           n_env = opts$n_env, step = step_opts$step,
                           max_search = step_opts$max_search)
  ## derivative (numeric if not supplied) -- validate the user one first
  fun_deriv <- ars_make_derivative(derivative, fun_log, lower, upper)
  if (!is.null(derivative)) {
    ars_validate_deriv(derivative, fun_log, Tk)
    fun_deriv <- function(x) as.numeric(derivative(x))
  }

  ## --- run the sampler -------------------------------------------------------
  if (verbose) message("ars: starting with |T| = ", length(Tk))
  res <- ars_sample_core(fun_log, fun_deriv, n, lower, upper, Tk,
                         opts$max_iter, opts$tol, opts$concavity_tol,
                         opts$verbose)

  out <- res$samples
  attr(out, "n_proposals") <- res$n_prop
  attr(out, "n_accepted")  <- res$n_acc
  attr(out, "acceptance_rate") <- res$n_acc / res$n_prop
  attr(out, "n_abscissae") <- res$n_abscissae
  attr(out, "abscissae")   <- res$abscissae
  attr(out, "domain")      <- c(lower, upper)
  out
}


## =============================================================================
## 8. FORMAL TESTING
## =============================================================================
##
## Strategy for testing a *stochastic* routine against known truth:
##
##   The output is random, so a test that compares "the sample" with "truth"
##   must never depend on a single draw.  Two complementary layers are used:
##
##   (A) Distributional tests with *fixed seeds*.  Because the seed is fixed,
##       the sample is a deterministic function of the code, so the test is
##       reproducible (a genuine regression test) while still being a valid
##       statistical test of correctness.  Standard tests are applied:
##         * Kolmogorov-Smirnov  (against the exact CDF)   -> p-value
##         * moment checks       (|mean-mean|/SE < 3, etc.) -> z-scores
##         * support / range checks                          -> hard pass/fail
##       A test "PASSES" only if p > 0.01 (KS) and all moment z-scores are
##       within +/- 4, and all hard checks hold.  Using a fixed seed keeps the
##       suite free of flaky failures while still detecting real errors (a
##       broken sampler fails these tests overwhelmingly).
##
##   (B) Assertion tests for the deterministic helpers (hull construction,
##       envelope sampling, validation) where the answer is known exactly or
##       can be checked by an invariant (e.g. "the envelope is above the
##       density everywhere").
##
## Every test prints "TEST_NAME: PASS" or "TEST_NAME: FAIL" as required, with
## the mean/sd statistics, so the output is clear and interpretable.

## Global test recorder ------------------------------------------------------
.arstest <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

ars_test_init <- function() {
  .arstest$results <- list()
  invisible(NULL)
}

## Report one test outcome in the required format.
##   name       : short test identifier (printed verbatim)
##   passed     : logical
##   detail     : optional extra one-line message
##   stats      : optional named list of "mean"/"sd" etc. to print
ars_test_report <- function(name, passed, stats = list(), detail = NULL) {
  status <- if (isTRUE(passed)) "PASS" else "FAIL"
  cat(sprintf("%s: %s\n", name, status))
  if (length(stats) > 0L) {
    parts <- vapply(names(stats), function(nm) {
      v <- stats[[nm]]
      if (is.numeric(v)) sprintf("%s=%.4f", nm, v) else sprintf("%s=%s", nm, v)
    }, character(1))
    cat("    ", paste(parts, collapse = "  "), "\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (!is.null(detail) && nzchar(detail))
    cat("    ", detail, "\n", sep = "")
  .arstest$results[[length(.arstest$results) + 1L]] <-
    list(name = name, passed = isTRUE(passed))
  invisible(isTRUE(passed))
}

## Helper: summarise a sample.
ars_test_stats <- function(x) list(mean = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x))

## KS test against an exact CDF; returns list(p, statistic). Robust to ties.
ars_test_ks <- function(x, cdf) {
  r <- stats::ks.test(x, cdf)
  list(p = r$p.value, statistic = as.numeric(r$statistic))
}

## Compare sample moments to truth using normal-approximation z-scores.
##   z_mean  = (mean(x) - mu) / (sigma / sqrt(n))
##   z_sd    = (sd(x)   - sigma) / (sigma / sqrt(2 n))
ars_test_moments <- function(x, mu, sigma) {
  n <- length(x)
  z_mean <- (mean(x) - mu) / (sigma / sqrt(n))
  z_sd   <- (stats::sd(x) - sigma) / (sigma / sqrt(2 * n))
  list(z_mean = z_mean, z_sd = z_sd)
}


## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Individual test cases
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Deterministic helper: hull construction & envelope property.
##    For a normal log-density we know h(x) = -x^2/2.  The tangent envelope
##    must (a) touch h at the abscissae, (b) lie above h between them.
ars_test_helpers <- function() {
  h  <- function(x) -0.5 * x^2
  dh <- function(x) -x
  Tk <- c(-2, -0.4, 0.9, 2.5)
  hh <- h(Tk); dd <- dh(Tk)
  hull <- ars_build_hull(Tk, hh, dd, -Inf, Inf)

  ## (a) envelope touches h at the abscissae
  e_at <- ars_eval_hull(Tk, hull$env)
  touch_ok <- all(abs(e_at - hh) < 1e-10)

  ## (b) envelope >= h on a dense grid
  grid <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 2001)
  env  <- ars_eval_hull(grid, hull$env)
  env_ok <- all(env >= h(grid) - 1e-10)

  ## (c) squeeze <= h everywhere (chords under a concave function)
  sq <- ars_eval_hull(grid, hull$squeeze)
  inside <- is.finite(sq)
  sq_ok <- all(sq[inside] <= h(grid)[inside] + 1e-10)

  pass <- touch_ok && env_ok && sq_ok
  ars_test_report(
    "HELPER_HULL_ENVELOPE", pass,
    stats = list(max_env_violation = max(h(grid) - env),
                 max_squeeze_violation = max(sq[inside] - h(grid)[inside])),
    detail = sprintf("tangent-touch=%s, envelope-above-density=%s, squeeze-below-density=%s",
                     touch_ok, env_ok, sq_ok)
  )
  pass
}

## 2. Deterministic helper: sampling from a piecewise-exponential envelope
##    must reproduce the envelope's probability mass per interval.
ars_test_env_sampler <- function() {
  h  <- function(x) -0.5 * x^2
  dh <- function(x) -x
  Tk <- c(-1.5, -0.2, 1.0)
  hull <- ars_build_hull(Tk, h(Tk), dh(Tk), -Inf, Inf)
  x <- ars_sample_env(hull, 200000)
  ## mass per interval from the closed form
  logmass <- ars_piece_logmass(hull$env)
  target_p <- exp(logmass - max(logmass)); target_p <- target_p / sum(target_p)
  idx <- ars_interval_index(x, hull$env$bounds)
  obs_p <- as.numeric(table(factor(idx, levels = seq_along(target_p)))) / length(x)
  ## chi-square goodness of fit on the interval proportions
  chisq <- sum((obs_p - target_p)^2 / target_p)
  pass <- chisq < stats::qchisq(0.99, df = length(target_p) - 1)
  ars_test_report(
    "HELPER_ENVELOPE_SAMPLER", pass,
    stats = list(mean = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x), chisq = chisq),
    detail = sprintf("interval proportions match envelope mass (chi-square=%.2f)", chisq)
  )
  pass
}

## 3. Deterministic tests: input validation must reject bad inputs.
ars_test_validation <- function() {
  expect_error <- function(expr) {
    r <- tryCatch({ force(expr); FALSE },
                  error = function(e) TRUE)
    r
  }
  checks <- c(
    neg_n        = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = -5)),
    zero_n       = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 0)),
    frac_n       = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 2.5)),
    nonfun       = expect_error(ars("not a function", n = 10)),
    bad_domain   = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 10, lower = 1, upper = -1)),
    no_finite    = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 10, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf, x0 = NULL,
                                    x0_step = 1)),
    x0_outside   = expect_error(ars(function(x) ifelse(x > 0 & x < 1, 1, 0), n = 10,
                                    lower = 0, upper = 1, x0 = c(-1, 2))),
    bad_log_fun  = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 10, log_fun = NA))
  )
  pass <- all(!checks)  ## all should have errored -> all TRUE
  ars_test_report(
    "INPUT_VALIDATION", all(checks),
    stats = list(checks_passed = sum(checks), checks_total = length(checks)),
    detail = paste(names(checks), checks, sep = "=", collapse = ", ")
  )
  all(checks)
}

## 4. Deterministic test: non-log-concave density must be rejected.
ars_test_nonconcave <- function() {
  ## A log-convex / bimodal density: mixture of two well-separated normals
  ## with unequal weights is *not* log-concave.
  bimodal <- function(x) 0.5 * dnorm(x, -3, 0.5) + 0.5 * dnorm(x, 3, 0.5)
  err <- tryCatch({ ars(bimodal, n = 50, seed = 1); FALSE },
                  error = function(e) TRUE)
  msg <- tryCatch({ ars(bimodal, n = 50, seed = 1); "" },
                  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
  is_concave_msg <- grepl("log-concave", msg, ignore.case = TRUE)
  ars_test_report(
    "NON_LOG_CONCAVE_REJECTED", err,
    detail = if (err) sprintf("raised: %s", substr(msg, 1, 90))
             else "bimodal density was NOT rejected"
  )
  err
}

## 5. Normal distribution: full statistical test against known truth.
ars_test_normal <- function(n = 5000, seed = 42) {
  mu <- 2; sigma <- 3
  x <- ars(dnorm, n = n, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf,
           derivative = function(x) -(x - mu) / sigma^2,
           x0 = mu, seed = seed,
           fun = NULL)  # placeholder to be overwritten below
  x
}

## (redefined properly; the silly placeholder above is never called)
ars_test_normal <- function(n = 5000, seed = 42) {
  mu <- 2; sigma <- 3
  ## Use dnorm with parameters via a closure; supply the analytic derivative.
  target <- function(x) dnorm(x, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
  deriv  <- function(x) -(x - mu) / sigma^2
  x <- ars(target, n = n, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf,
           derivative = deriv, x0 = mu, seed = seed)
  st <- ars_test_stats(x)
  ks <- ars_test_ks(x, function(q) pnorm(q, mean = mu, sd = sigma))
  mom <- ars_test_moments(x, mu, sigma)
  pass <- ks$p > 0.01 && abs(mom$z_mean) < 4 && abs(mom$z_sd) < 4
  ars_test_report(
    "NORMAL", pass,
    stats = list(mean = st$mean, sd = st$sd, target_mean = mu,
                 target_sd = sigma, ks_p = ks$p,
                 z_mean = mom$z_mean, z_sd = mom$z_sd),
    detail = sprintf("KS p=%.3f (should be > 0.01); z_mean=%.2f, z_sd=%.2f (|z|<4)",
                     ks$p, mom$z_mean, mom$z_sd)
  )
  list(pass = pass, samples = x)
}

## 6. Exponential distribution (one-sided support, numeric derivative path).
ars_test_exponential <- function(n = 5000, seed = 7, rate = 0.5) {
  target <- function(x) dexp(x, rate = rate)
  ## no analytic derivative supplied -> numerical differentiation is exercised;
  ## support is one-sided so we must give a starting point.
  x <- ars(target, n = n, lower = 0, upper = Inf, x0 = c(1, 3, 6),
           seed = seed)
  st <- ars_test_stats(x)
  ks <- ars_test_ks(x, function(q) pexp(q, rate = rate))
  mom <- ars_test_moments(x, 1 / rate, 1 / rate)
  support_ok <- all(x >= 0)
  pass <- support_ok && ks$p > 0.01 && abs(mom$z_mean) < 4 && abs(mom$z_sd) < 4
  ars_test_report(
    "EXPONENTIAL", pass,
    stats = list(mean = st$mean, sd = st$sd, target_mean = 1 / rate,
                 target_sd = 1 / rate, ks_p = ks$p,
                 z_mean = mom$z_mean, z_sd = mom$z_sd),
    detail = sprintf("support>=0=%s; KS p=%.3f; z_mean=%.2f; z_sd=%.2f",
                     support_ok, ks$p, mom$z_mean, mom$z_sd)
  )
  list(pass = pass, samples = x)
}

## 7. Uniform distribution on a bounded interval (finite both bounds).
ars_test_uniform <- function(n = 4000, seed = 11) {
  target <- function(x) ifelse(x >= -1 & x <= 2, 1, 0)
  x <- ars(target, n = n, lower = -1, upper = 2, x0 = c(-0.5, 0.5, 1.5),
           seed = seed)
  st <- ars_test_stats(x)
  ks <- ars_test_ks(x, function(q) punif(q, -1, 2))
  mom <- ars_test_moments(x, 0.5, sqrt(3))
  range_ok <- all(x >= -1 & x <= 2)
  pass <- range_ok && ks$p > 0.01 && abs(mom$z_mean) < 4
  ars_test_report(
    "UNIFORM", pass,
    stats = list(mean = st$mean, sd = st$sd, target_mean = 0.5,
                 target_sd = sqrt(3), ks_p = ks$p),
    detail = sprintf("range in [-1,2]=%s; KS p=%.3f", range_ok, ks$p)
  )
  list(pass = pass, samples = x)
}

## 8. Gamma(shape = 3, rate = 1) -- known truth, log-concave only for
##    shape >= 1, exercises the numerical derivative with a one-sided support.
ars_test_gamma <- function(n = 5000, seed = 13) {
  shape <- 3; rate <- 1
  target <- function(x) dgamma(x, shape = shape, rate = rate)
  x <- ars(target, n = n, lower = 0, upper = Inf, x0 = c(0.5, 2, 5),
           seed = seed)
  st <- ars_test_stats(x)
  ks <- ars_test_ks(x, function(q) pgamma(q, shape = shape, rate = rate))
  mom <- ars_test_moments(x, shape / rate, sqrt(shape) / rate)
  pass <- all(x >= 0) && ks$p > 0.01 && abs(mom$z_mean) < 4 && abs(mom$z_sd) < 4
  ars_test_report(
    "GAMMA", pass,
    stats = list(mean = st$mean, sd = st$sd, target_mean = shape / rate,
                 target_sd = sqrt(shape) / rate, ks_p = ks$p),
    detail = sprintf("KS p=%.3f; z_mean=%.2f; z_sd=%.2f", ks$p, mom$z_mean, mom$z_sd)
  )
  list(pass = pass, samples = x)
}

## 9. log_fun = TRUE and unnormalised density: log-density known only up to a
##    constant.  Sampling must still match the truth (constants cancel).
ars_test_log_fun <- function(n = 4000, seed = 17) {
  ## unnormalised log-density of N(0, 1) shifted by an arbitrary constant 100
  log_target <- function(x) dnorm(x, log = TRUE) + 100
  x <- ars(log_target, n = n, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf, log_fun = TRUE,
           x0 = c(-1, 0, 1), seed = seed)
  st <- ars_test_stats(x)
  ks <- ars_test_ks(x, pnorm)
  mom <- ars_test_moments(x, 0, 1)
  pass <- ks$p > 0.01 && abs(mom$z_mean) < 4 && abs(mom$z_sd) < 4
  ars_test_report(
    "LOG_FUN_UNNORMALISED", pass,
    stats = list(mean = st$mean, sd = st$sd, ks_p = ks$p),
    detail = sprintf("unnormalised log-density, KS p=%.3f", ks$p)
  )
  list(pass = pass, samples = x)
}

## 10. Reproducibility: same seed -> identical samples.
ars_test_reproducible <- function() {
  f <- function(x) dnorm(x)
  a <- ars(f, n = 100, seed = 99)
  b <- ars(f, n = 100, seed = 99)
  pass <- identical(a, b)
  ars_test_report(
    "REPRODUCIBILITY", pass,
    stats = list(mean = mean(a), sd = stats::sd(a)),
    detail = "same seed gives identical output"
  )
  pass
}

## 11. Acceptance-rate sanity: the sampler must actually reject sometimes and
##     must be reasonably efficient (not accept everything blindly).
ars_test_acceptance <- function() {
  x <- ars(function(x) dnorm(x, 0, 1), n = 2000, seed = 5)
  rate <- attr(x, "acceptance_rate")
  pass <- !is.null(rate) && rate > 0.05 && rate <= 1
  ars_test_report(
    "ACCEPTANCE_RATE", pass,
    stats = list(mean = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x), acceptance_rate = rate),
    detail = sprintf("acceptance rate = %.3f |T| = %d",
                     rate, attr(x, "n_abscissae"))
  )
  pass
}


## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## The user-facing `test()` function
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#'
#' Run the formal test-suite for the adaptive rejection sampler.
#'
#' Prints "TEST_NAME: PASS" / "TEST_NAME: FAIL" for each test together with
#' mean/sd statistics.  Optionally writes the normal and exponential samples to
#' files (default: /app/normal_samples.txt and /app/exponential_samples.txt).
#'
#' @param write_files  Write sample files (default TRUE).
#' @param dir          Directory for sample files (default "/app", falling back
#'                     to the working directory if /app is not writable).
#' @return Invisibly, TRUE if all tests passed, FALSE otherwise.
#' @export
test <- function(write_files = TRUE, dir = "/app") {
  ars_test_init()
  cat("================================================================\n")
  cat("  ARS (Gilks & Wild 1992) formal test suite\n")
  cat("================================================================\n\n")

  ## ---- deterministic helper tests ----
  cat("-- deterministic helper tests --\n")
  ars_test_helpers()
  ars_test_env_sampler()
  ars_test_validation()
  ars_test_nonconcave()
  ars_test_reproducible()

  ## ---- statistical tests against known truth ----
  cat("\n-- statistical tests against known distributions --\n")
  norm <- ars_test_normal()
  expo <- ars_test_exponential()
  ars_test_uniform()
  ars_test_gamma()
  ars_test_log_fun()
  ars_test_acceptance()

  ## ---- write sample files ----
  if (write_files) {
    cat("\n-- sample files --\n")
    odir <- if (dir.exists(dir) && file.access(dir, 2) == 0) dir else getwd()
    fnorm <- file.path(odir, "normal_samples.txt")
    fexpo <- file.path(odir, "exponential_samples.txt")
    write.table(norm$samples, fnorm, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
    write.table(expo$samples, fexpo, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf("Sample file: %s (%d samples, mean=%.4f, sd=%.4f)\n",
                fnorm, length(norm$samples), mean(norm$samples), sd(norm$samples)))
    cat(sprintf("Sample file: %s (%d samples, mean=%.4f, sd=%.4f)\n",
                fexpo, length(expo$samples), mean(expo$samples), sd(expo$samples)))
  }

  ## ---- summary ----
  res <- .arstest$results
  n_pass <- sum(vapply(res, function(r) r$passed, logical(1)))
  n_all  <- length(res)
  cat("\n----------------------------------------------------------------\n")
  cat(sprintf("SUMMARY: %d / %d tests passed\n", n_pass, n_all))
  cat("----------------------------------------------------------------\n")
  invisible(n_pass == n_all)
}


## =============================================================================
## Command-line entry point:  Rscript ars.R
## =============================================================================
if (sys.nframe() == 0L && !interactive()) {
  ok <- test()
  if (!isTRUE(ok)) quit(status = 1L)
}
"}
