<｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter name="content" string="true">## =============================================================================
##  ars.R  --  Adaptive Rejection Sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992)
##
##  Implementation of the adaptive rejection sampler of
##      Gilks, W. R. & Wild, P. (1992). Adaptive rejection sampling for Gibbs
##      sampling. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C (Applied
##      Statistics), 41(2), 337-348.
##
##  The sampler targets an arbitrary *log-concave* (possibly unnormalised)
##  density on an interval of the real line.  It works entirely with the
##  log-density h(x) = log f(x) and maintains a piecewise-linear envelope
##  (upper hull) built from the tangents of h at the abscissae of an
##  "abscissae set" T_k, together with a piecewise-exponential squeezing
##  function (lower hull) built from the chords between consecutive abscissae.
##  Points are proposed from the envelope and are accepted with probability
##  exp(h - envelope); whenever the squeeze test fails and the point is not
##  accepted it is added to T_k, sharpening both hulls.
##
##  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
##  File layout (modular design)
##  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
##   Section 1  Input validation helpers      (small, focused checks)
##   Section 2  Log-density / derivative      (numerical derivatives)
##   Section 3  Abscissae-set management      (insertion, sorting, search)
##   Section 4  Hull construction             (envelope + squeeze as exp lines)
##   Section 5  Hull evaluation / sampling    from the envelope
##   Section 6  Core sampling loop            (+ log-concavity checks)
##   Section 7  User-facing `ars()`           (validation, dispatch, output)
##   Section 8  Testing framework `test()`    (formal tests vs known truth)
##
##  Naming conventions
##  ------------------
##  * internal helpers are prefixed `ars_` and use lower_snake_case verbs:
##        ars_validate_*  input validation      ars_make_*   build closures
##        ars_build_*     construct objects     ars_eval_*   evaluate objects
##        ars_test_*      test cases/utilities  ars_check_*  runtime checks
##  * hull objects are plain lists with a documented structure:
##        list(intercepts, slopes, bounds)
##    where piece j is the exponential of  intercepts[j] + slopes[j] * x
##    on  (bounds[j], bounds[j+1]).
##  * all public functions return plain R objects (a numeric sample vector, for
##    `ars()`, with descriptive attributes).
## =============================================================================


## =============================================================================
## 1. INPUT VALIDATION HELPERS
## =============================================================================

## Throw a uniform, informative error (no call, no trailing noise).
ars_stop <- function(...) {
  stop(paste0(...), call. = FALSE)
}

## Is `x` a single, finite, non-NA numeric value?
ars_is_number <- function(x) {
  is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1L && !is.na(x) && is.finite(x)
}

## Is `x` a single logical value (TRUE / FALSE, not NA)?
ars_is_flag <- function(x) {
  is.logical(x) && length(x) == 1L && !is.na(x)
}

## Validate the target: an R function that is vectorised in its first argument.
ars_validate_fun <- function(fun) {
  if (missing(fun) || is.null(fun))
    ars_stop("`fun` must be supplied: a (vectorised) function evaluating the ",
             "unnormalised density of the target distribution.")
  if (!is.function(fun))
    ars_stop("`fun` must be a function (e.g. `dnorm`, `dexp` or ", 
             "`function(x) ...`); got an object of class '",
             paste(class(fun), collapse = "/"), "'.")

  ## Probe the function once to make sure it is vectorised and usable.
  probe <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(fun(c(-1.2345, 0, 0.6789))),
    error = function(e) ars_stop("`fun` could not be evaluated on a numeric ",
                                 "vector: ", conditionMessage(e))
  )
  if (!is.numeric(probe))
    ars_stop("`fun` must return a numeric vector; it returned class '",
             paste(class(probe), collapse = "/"), "'.")
  if (length(probe) != 3L)
    ars_stop("`fun` must be vectorised: evaluating it on 3 inputs returned ",
             length(probe), " value(s). Wrap scalar-only functions with ",
             "Vectorize().")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

## Validate a single sample size.
ars_validate_n <- function(n) {
  if (!is.numeric(n) || length(n) != 1L || is.na(n))
    ars_stop("`n` must be a single non-missing number.")
  if (!is.finite(n))
    ars_stop("`n` must be finite; got ", n, ".")
  if (n < 1)
    ars_stop("`n` must be a positive integer (number of samples); got ",
             format(n), ".")
  if (n != as.integer(n))
    ars_stop("`n` must be a whole number; got ", format(n), ".")
  if (n > 1e8)
    ars_stop("`n` is unreasonably large (> 1e8); refusing to allocate.")
  as.integer(n)
}

## Validate the (lower, upper) domain.  -Inf/Inf are allowed (the natural
## choice for unbounded support); at least one bound must be finite so that
## initial abscissae can be located.
ars_validate_domain <- function(lower, upper) {
  ok <- function(z) is.numeric(z) && length(z) == 1L && !is.na(z)
  if (!ok(lower))
    ars_stop("`lower` must be a single number (use -Inf for an unbounded ",
             "left support).")
  if (!ok(upper))
    ars_stop("`upper` must be a single number (use Inf for an unbounded ",
             "right support).")
  if (lower >= upper)
    ars_stop("`lower` (", lower, ") must be strictly less than `upper` (",
             upper, ").")
  if (!is.finite(lower) && !is.finite(upper))
    ars_stop("At least one of `lower`/`upper` must be finite so that the ",
             "initial abscissae can be located.")
  c(lower = as.numeric(lower), upper = as.numeric(upper))
}

## Validate user-supplied starting abscissae against the domain and support.
ars_validate_x0 <- function(x0, lower, upper, fun_log) {
  if (is.null(x0)) return(NULL)
  if (!is.numeric(x0) || length(x0) < 1L)
    ars_stop("`x0` must be a numeric vector of at least one starting abscissa.")
  if (anyNA(x0) || any(!is.finite(x0)))
    ars_stop("`x0` must contain only finite numbers.")
  x0 <- sort(unique(as.numeric(x0)))
  if (any(x0 <= lower) || any(x0 >= upper))
    ars_stop("All starting abscissae `x0` must lie strictly inside ",
             "(`lower`, `upper`) = (", lower, ", ", upper, ").")
  hv <- fun_log(x0)
  bad <- !is.finite(hv)
  if (any(bad))
    ars_stop("The log-density is not finite at starting abscissa(e): ",
             paste(signif(x0[bad], 6), collapse = ", "),
             ". These points are outside the support of the target.")
  x0
}

## Validate a user-supplied derivative function.
ars_validate_deriv <- function(deriv, x0) {
  if (is.null(deriv)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (!is.function(deriv))
    ars_stop("`derivative` must be NULL or a (vectorised) function.")
  probe <- tryCatch(deriv(x0), error = function(e)
    ars_stop("`derivative` could not be evaluated: ", conditionMessage(e)))
  if (!is.numeric(probe) || length(probe) != length(x0))
    ars_stop("`derivative` must be vectorised and return one value per input ",
             "(got ", length(probe), " value(s) for ", length(x0), " input(s)).")
  if (any(!is.finite(probe)))
    ars_stop("`derivative` returned non-finite value(s) at the starting ",
             "abscissae.")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

## Validate the initial-abscissae search parameters.
ars_validate_search <- function(step, max_search) {
  if (!ars_is_number(step) || step <= 0)
    ars_stop("`x0_step` must be a single positive number; got ",
             paste(format(step), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!ars_is_number(max_search) || max_search < 1 ||
      max_search != as.integer(max_search))
    ars_stop("`max_search` must be a positive integer; got ",
             paste(format(max_search), collapse = ","), ".")
  list(step = as.numeric(step), max_search = as.integer(max_search))
}

## Validate the remaining numerical / logical options.
ars_validate_opts <- function(n_env, max_iter, tol, concavity_tol, verbose) {
  if (!ars_is_number(n_env) || n_env < 3 || n_env != as.integer(n_env))
    ars_stop("`n_env` (initial abscissae count) must be an integer >= 3; got ",
             paste(format(n_env), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!ars_is_number(max_iter) || max_iter < 1 || max_iter != as.integer(max_iter))
    ars_stop("`max_iter` must be a positive integer; got ",
             paste(format(max_iter), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!ars_is_number(tol) || tol < 0)
    ars_stop("`tol` must be a non-negative number; got ",
             paste(format(tol), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!ars_is_number(concavity_tol) || concavity_tol < 0)
    ars_stop("`concavity_tol` must be a non-negative number; got ",
             paste(format(concavity_tol), collapse = ","), ".")
  if (!ars_is_flag(verbose))
    ars_stop("`verbose` must be TRUE or FALSE.")
  list(n_env = as.integer(n_env), max_iter = as.integer(max_iter),
       tol = as.numeric(tol), concavity_tol = as.numeric(concavity_tol),
       verbose = verbose)
}


## =============================================================================
## 2. LOG-DENSITY AND DERIVATIVE
## =============================================================================

## Build the log-density h(x) = log f(x) from the user's density.
##   * `log_fun = TRUE`  : `fun` already returns log f.
##   * `log_fun = FALSE` : `fun` returns f; take logs here.
## NaN results are mapped to -Inf so that "outside the support" is handled.
ars_make_log_density <- function(fun, log_fun) {
  force(fun); force(log_fun)
  function(x) {
    v <- fun(x)
    h <- if (log_fun) v else log(v)
    h[is.nan(h)] <- -Inf
    h
  }
}

## Numerically differentiate the log-density at a single point (central
## difference, step scaled to |x| and kept inside the domain).
ars_num_deriv1 <- function(fun_log, x, lower, upper) {
  h <- fun_log(x)
  if (!is.finite(h))
    ars_stop("Cannot differentiate the log-density at x = ", signif(x, 8),
             ": log-density is not finite there.")
  dx <- 1e-5 * max(1, abs(x))
  xl <- x - dx; xr <- x + dx
  if (is.finite(lower) && xl <= lower) { xl <- x; dx <- xr - x }
  if (is.finite(upper) && xr >= upper) { xr <- x; dx <- x - xl }
  if (xl == xr)
    ars_stop("Cannot numerically differentiate the log-density at x = ",
             signif(x, 8), ": the domain is too narrow.")
  hl <- fun_log(xl); hr <- fun_log(xr)
  if (!is.finite(hl) || !is.finite(hr))
    ars_stop("Numerical differentiation of the log-density failed near x = ",
             signif(x, 8), " (log-density not finite on a neighbourhood).")
  (hr - hl) / (xr - xl)
}

## Return a vectorised derivative function of x.
ars_make_derivative <- function(deriv, fun_log, lower, upper) {
  if (!is.null(deriv)) {
    force(deriv)
    return(function(x) as.numeric(deriv(x)))
  }
  force(fun_log); force(lower); force(upper)
  function(x) vapply(as.numeric(x),
                     function(xi) ars_num_deriv1(fun_log, xi, lower, upper),
                     numeric(1))
}


## =============================================================================
## 3. ABSCISSAE-SET MANAGEMENT
## =============================================================================

## Insert `x_new` into the sorted abscissae vector `Tk`, keeping it sorted and
## unique.  Coincident points are ignored.
ars_insert_abscissa <- function(Tk, x_new, tol = 1e-10) {
  if (any(abs(Tk - x_new) <= tol * max(1, abs(x_new)))) return(Tk)
  sort(c(Tk, x_new))
}

## Compute log-density and derivative at every abscissa of `Tk`, with the
## first log-concavity check (the tangent slopes must be non-increasing).
## Returns list(x = Tk, h = h(Tk), dh = h'(Tk)).
ars_eval_abscissae <- function(Tk, fun_log, fun_deriv, tol) {
  h <- fun_log(Tk)
  if (any(!is.finite(h)))
    ars_stop("The log-density is not finite at abscissa(e) ",
             paste(signif(Tk[!is.finite(h)], 6), collapse = ", "),
             ". Those points lie outside the support of the target; supply ",
             "starting abscissae `x0` inside the support.")
  dh <- fun_deriv(Tk)
  if (length(dh) > 1L) {
    dif <- diff(dh)
    if (any(dif > tol)) {
      i <- which(dif > tol)
      ars_stop("Density is not log-concave: the derivative of the log-density ",
               "increases between abscissae ",
               paste(sprintf("%g->%g", Tk[i], Tk[i + 1L]), collapse = ", "),
               " (increase = ", signif(max(dif), 4), " > tol = ", tol, "). ",
               "ARS requires a log-concave target.")
    }
  }
  list(x = Tk, h = h, dh = dh)
}

## Locate an initial abscissae set of (about) `n_env` points with finite
## log-density strictly inside the domain.
ars_find_abscissae <- function(fun_log, lower, upper, x0, n_env, step,
                               max_search) {
  finite_both <- is.finite(lower) && is.finite(upper)

  if (!is.null(x0)) {
    Tk <- x0
  } else if (finite_both) {
    Tk <- seq(lower + (upper - lower) / (n_env + 1L),
              upper - (upper - lower) / (n_env + 1L),
              length.out = n_env)
  } else {
    ## One-sided / unbounded domains: scan outwards from an interior point.
    centre <- if (is.finite(lower)) lower + step else upper - step
    cand <- centre + step * (0:(max_search - 1L))
    cand <- cand[cand > lower & cand < upper]
    ok <- is.finite(fun_log(cand))
    cand <- cand[ok]
    if (length(cand) < 2L)
      ars_stop("Could not find two abscissae with finite log-density near ",
               signif(centre, 6), "; please supply `x0`.")
    Tk <- cand
  }

  ## Clean up: keep points strictly inside the domain with finite log-density.
  Tk <- sort(unique(as.numeric(Tk)))
  Tk <- Tk[Tk > lower & Tk < upper]
  Tk <- Tk[is.finite(fun_log(Tk))]

  ## Grow outwards (geometrically) until at least `n_env` points are available.
  grow <- function(side) {
    last <- if (side == "right") max(Tk) else min(Tk)
    dir  <- if (side == "right") 1 else -1
    for (k in seq_len(max_search)) {
      cand <- last + dir * step * 2^(k - 1L)
      if (cand <= lower || cand >= upper) break
      if (is.finite(fun_log(cand))) {
        Tk <- sort(unique(c(Tk, cand)))
        last <- cand
      }
      if (length(Tk) >= n_env) break
    }
    Tk
  }
  if (length(Tk) < n_env) Tk <- grow("right")
  if (length(Tk) < n_env) Tk <- grow("left")

  if (length(Tk) < 2L)
    ars_stop("Unable to locate at least two abscissae with finite ",
             "log-density inside (", lower, ", ", upper, "). Check the domain ",
             "and the support of the target, or pass `x0`.")
  Tk
}


## =============================================================================
## 4. HULL CONSTRUCTION
## =============================================================================
##
## With abscissae x_1 < ... < x_k and tangents l_i(x) = h_i + h'_i (x - x_i),
##
##   upper hull  u_k(x) = l_i(x) on (z_{i-1}, z_i)              [envelope]
##   lower hull  L_k(x) = chord between (x_i, h_i), (x_{i+1}, h_{i+1})
##                        on (x_i, x_{i+1})                      [squeeze]
##
## where z_0 = lower, z_k = upper and z_i (i = 1..k-1) is the intersection of
## tangents l_i and l_{i+1}:
##   z_i = (h_{i+1} - h_i - h'_{i+1} x_{i+1} + h'_i x_i) / (h'_i - h'_{i+1}).
##
## Both hulls are piecewise exponentials of straight lines, stored as
## list(intercepts, slopes, bounds): piece j is valid on
## (bounds[j], bounds[j+1]).

## Intersection abscissae of consecutive tangents.
ars_intersections <- function(x, h, dh) {
  k <- length(x)
  if (k < 2L) return(numeric(0))
  i <- seq_len(k - 1L)
  denom <- dh[i] - dh[i + 1L]
  z <- (h[i + 1L] - h[i] - dh[i + 1L] * x[i + 1L] + dh[i] * x[i]) / denom
  ## Parallel tangents (zero curvature): use the interval mid-point instead.
  bad <- !is.finite(z)
  if (any(bad)) z[bad] <- (x[i][bad] + x[i + 1L][bad]) / 2
  z
}

## Build the envelope and squeeze hulls from an abscissae set.
ars_build_hull <- function(x, h, dh, lower, upper) {
  ## envelope: tangent lines  a + b x,  b = h', a = h - h' x
  a_tan <- h - dh * x
  b_tan <- dh

  ## squeeze: chords between consecutive abscissae
  if (length(x) >= 2L) {
    s <- diff(h) / diff(x)
    a_chord <- h[-length(h)] - s * x[-length(x)]
  } else {
    s <- numeric(0); a_chord <- numeric(0)
  }

  z <- ars_intersections(x, h, dh)

  list(
    env     = list(intercepts = a_tan, slopes = b_tan,
                   bounds = c(lower, z, upper)),
    squeeze = list(intercepts = a_chord, slopes = s,
                   bounds = c(lower, x, upper)),
    z = z, x = x, h = h, dh = dh, lower = lower, upper = upper
  )
}


## =============================================================================
## 5. HULL EVALUATION AND ENVELOPE SAMPLING
## =============================================================================

## Interval index (1..m) of each x, 0 when outside the bounds.
ars_interval_index <- function(x, bounds) {
  idx <- findInterval(x, bounds, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
  idx[idx < 1L | idx > length(bounds) - 1L] <- 0L
  idx
}

## Evaluate a piecewise-exponential hull on the log scale at arbitrary x.
ars_eval_hull <- function(x, hull) {
  a <- hull$intercepts; b <- hull$slopes
  idx <- ars_interval_index(x, hull$bounds)
  out <- rep(-Inf, length(x))
  inside <- idx > 0L
  if (any(inside)) {
    ii <- idx[inside]
    out[inside] <- a[ii] + b[ii] * x[inside]
  }
  out
}

## Log of the probability mass of every piece of a piecewise-exponential hull.
## The integral of exp(a + b x) over [lo, hi] has a closed form.
ars_piece_logmass <- function(hull) {
  a <- hull$intercepts; b <- hull$slopes; bd <- hull$bounds
  lo <- bd[-length(bd)]; hi <- bd[-1L]
  anti <- function(z) {
    out <- numeric(length(z))
    nz <- b != 0
    out[nz]  <- exp(a[nz] + b[nz] * z[nz]) / b[nz]
    out[!nz] <- exp(a[!nz]) * z[!nz]
    out
  }
  log(pmax(anti(hi) - anti(lo), .Machine$double.xmin))
}

## Sample `m` points from the piecewise-exponential envelope:
## choose an interval with probability proportional to its mass, then invert
## the (truncated) exponential CDF inside that interval.  Exactly correct.
ars_sample_env <- function(hull, m) {
  a <- hull$intercepts; b <- hull$slopes; bd <- hull$bounds
  logmass <- ars_piece_logmass(hull)
  j <- sample.int(length(logmass), size = m, replace = TRUE,
                  prob = exp(logmass - max(logmass)))
  lo <- bd[j]; hi <- bd[j + 1L]; aa <- a[j]; bb <- b[j]
  u <- stats::runif(m)
  x <- numeric(m)
  nz <- bb != 0
  x[nz] <- log(exp(bb[nz] * lo[nz]) +
                 u[nz] * (exp(bb[nz] * hi[nz]) - exp(bb[nz] * lo[nz]))) / bb[nz]
  x[!nz] <- lo[!nz] + u[!nz] * (hi[!nz] - lo[!nz])   # flat piece: uniform
  pmin(pmax(x, pmin(lo, hi)), pmax(lo, hi))          # round-off guard
}


## =============================================================================
## 6. CORE SAMPLING LOOP
## =============================================================================

## Second log-concavity check: the tangent envelope must lie above the
## log-density everywhere on a dense grid built from the hull's boundaries.
ars_check_logconcavity <- function(fun_log, hull, lower, upper,
                                   concavity_tol) {
  bd <- sort(unique(hull$env$bounds[is.finite(hull$env$bounds)]))
  if (length(bd) < 2L) return(invisible(TRUE))
  grid <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(length(bd) - 1L), function(i)
    seq(bd[i], bd[i + 1L], length.out = 5L)), use.names = FALSE)
  grid <- unique(grid[grid > lower & grid < upper])
  if (length(grid) < 1L) return(invisible(TRUE))
  h <- fun_log(grid)
  e <- ars_eval_hull(grid, hull$env)
  viol <- which(is.finite(h) & is.finite(e) & (h > e + concavity_tol))
  if (length(viol) > 0L) {
    w <- viol[seq_len(min(3L, length(viol)))]
    ars_stop("Density is not log-concave: the log-density exceeds its tangent ",
             "envelope at x = ", paste(signif(grid[w], 6), collapse = ", "),
             " (excess = ", signif(max(h[viol] - e[viol]), 4), " > ",
             "concavity_tol = ", concavity_tol, "). ARS requires a ",
             "log-concave target.")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

## The core rejection-sampling loop (see Gilks & Wild 1992, Algorithm).
ars_sample_core <- function(fun_log, fun_deriv, n, lower, upper, Tk,
                            max_iter, tol, concavity_tol, verbose) {
  if (length(Tk) < 2L)
    ars_stop("Internal error: need at least 2 abscissae to start sampling.")

  ## initial evaluation + log-concavity check #1
  info <- ars_eval_abscissae(Tk, fun_log, fun_deriv, tol)
  Tk <- info$x; h <- info$h; dh <- info$dh
  hull <- ars_build_hull(Tk, h, dh, lower, upper)
  ars_check_logconcavity(fun_log, hull, lower, upper, concavity_tol)  # check #2

  samples <- numeric(n)
  n_done <- 0L; n_prop <- 0L; n_acc <- 0L; n_squeeze <- 0L
  it <- 0L
  ## safety limit: generous, and always at least 20 n proposals
  max_total <- max(max_iter, 20L * n)

  while (n_done < n) {
    it <- it + 1L
    if (it > max_total)
      ars_stop("Sampler failed to draw ", n, " accepted samples within ",
               max_total, " iterations (drawn = ", n_done, ", accepted = ",
               n_acc, "). The density may be only weakly log-concave; ",
               "consider supplying `x0`/`derivative` or increasing `max_iter`.")

    x_new <- ars_sample_env(hull, 1L)
    n_prop <- n_prop + 1L
    en <- ars_eval_hull(x_new, hull$env)
    lq <- ars_eval_hull(x_new, hull$squeeze)
    log_u <- log(stats::runif(1L))

    ## --- squeeze test: accept without touching the density (cheap path) -----
    if (is.finite(lq) && log_u <= lq - en) {
      n_acc <- n_acc + 1L; n_squeeze <- n_squeeze + 1L; n_done <- n_done + 1L
      samples[n_done] <- x_new
      next
    }

    ## --- full acceptance test ----------------------------------------------
    h_new <- fun_log(x_new)
    if (is.finite(h_new) && log_u <= (h_new - en)) {
      n_acc <- n_acc + 1L; n_done <- n_done + 1L
      samples[n_done] <- x_new
      next
    }

    ## --- reject and adapt ---------------------------------------------------
    ## Points outside the support carry no information: reject, no update.
    if (!is.finite(h_new)) next

    new_Tk <- ars_insert_abscissa(Tk, x_new)
    if (length(new_Tk) == length(Tk)) next   # coincident with existing point

    Tk <- new_Tk
    info <- ars_eval_abscissae(Tk, fun_log, fun_deriv, tol)  # check #1
    h <- info$h; dh <- info$dh
    hull <- ars_build_hull(Tk, h, dh, lower, upper)
    if (it %% 5L == 0L)
      ars_check_logconcavity(fun_log, hull, lower, upper, concavity_tol)

    if (verbose && it %% 1000L == 0L)
      message(sprintf("  [ars] it=%d drawn=%d accepted=%d |T|=%d",
                      it, n_done, n_acc, length(Tk)))
  }

  list(samples = samples, n_prop = n_prop, n_acc = n_acc,
       n_squeeze = n_squeeze, n_abscissae = length(Tk), abscissae = Tk)
}


## =============================================================================
## 7. USER-FACING `ars()`
## =============================================================================

#' Adaptive Rejection Sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992)
#'
#' Draw `n` independent samples from a target density f that is known up to a
#' normalising constant and is log-concave on its support.
#'
#' @param fun        (Vectorised) function computing the unnormalised density f.
#'                   Set `log_fun = TRUE` if it returns log f instead.
#' @param n          Number of samples to draw (positive whole number).
#' @param lower,upper  Support of the target.  `-Inf`/`Inf` are allowed; at
#'                   least one bound must be finite when `x0` is not supplied.
#' @param x0         Optional numeric vector of starting abscissae (strictly
#'                   inside (lower, upper), finite log-density required).
#' @param derivative Optional vectorised function for d/dx log f; if NULL, a
#'                   numerical derivative is used.
#' @param log_fun    Does `fun` return the log-density? (default FALSE)
#' @param n_env      Number of initial abscissae (>= 3).
#' @param x0_step    Scale used when searching for initial abscissae.
#' @param max_search Maximum number of search steps.
#' @param max_iter   Safety cap on the number of proposals.
#' @param tol        Derivative tolerance for the log-concavity check.
#' @param concavity_tol  Tolerance for the envelope concavity check.
#' @param seed       Optional integer seed.
#' @param verbose    Print progress messages?
#' @return A numeric vector of `n` samples, with attributes giving diagnostics
#'         (number of proposals, acceptance rate, final abscissae, ...).
#' @export
ars <- function(fun,
                n,
                lower = -Inf,
                upper = Inf,
                x0 = NULL,
                derivative = NULL,
                log_fun = FALSE,
                n_env = 10L,
                x0_step = 1,
                max_search = 50L,
                max_iter = 100000L,
                tol = 1e-6,
                concavity_tol = 1e-6,
                seed = NULL,
                verbose = FALSE) {

  ## --- validation (fail fast, with informative messages) --------------------
  ars_validate_fun(fun)
  n <- ars_validate_n(n)
  dom <- ars_validate_domain(lower, upper)
  lower <- dom[["lower"]]; upper <- dom[["upper"]]
  if (!ars_is_flag(log_fun))
    ars_stop("`log_fun` must be TRUE or FALSE.")
  opts <- ars_validate_opts(n_env, max_iter, tol, concavity_tol, verbose)
  search <- ars_validate_search(x0_step, max_search)

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    if (!ars_is_number(seed))
      ars_stop("`seed` must be NULL or a single finite number.")
    set.seed(as.integer(seed))
  }

  ## --- build h(x) and h'(x) -------------------------------------------------
  fun_log <- ars_make_log_density(fun, log_fun)

  if (!is.null(x0))
    x0 <- ars_validate_x0(x0, lower, upper, fun_log)

  ## initial abscissae
  Tk <- ars_find_abscissae(fun_log, lower, upper, x0,
                           n_env = opts$n_env, step = search$step,
                           max_search = search$max_search)
  if (!is.null(derivative))
    ars_validate_deriv(derivative, Tk)
  fun_deriv <- ars_make_derivative(derivative, fun_log, lower, upper)

  ## --- run the sampler ------------------------------------------------------
  if (verbose) message("ars: starting with |T| = ", length(Tk))
  res <- ars_sample_core(fun_log, fun_deriv, n, lower, upper, Tk,
                         opts$max_iter, opts$tol, opts$concavity_tol,
                         opts$verbose)

  out <- res$samples
  attr(out, "n_proposals")     <- res$n_prop
  attr(out, "n_accepted")      <- res$n_acc
  attr(out, "n_squeeze_accept") <- res$n_squeeze
  attr(out, "acceptance_rate") <- res$n_acc / res$n_prop
  attr(out, "n_abscissae")     <- res$n_abscissae
  attr(out, "abscissae")       <- res$abscissae
  attr(out, "domain")          <- c(lower, upper)
  out
}


## =============================================================================
## 8. FORMAL TESTING
## =============================================================================
##
## Testing a stochastic routine requires care.  The strategy used here is:
##
##   (A) Statistical tests against the *known truth*, run with a fixed seed.
##       A fixed seed makes the sample a deterministic function of the code,
##       so the suite is fully reproducible (a real regression test) while
##       remaining a valid statistical test of correctness.  The following
##       checks are applied to every distributional test:
##         * Kolmogorov-Smirnov test vs the exact CDF  -> p-value > 0.01
##         * moment checks: |z_mean| < 4 and |z_sd| < 4 where
##               z_mean = (mean - mu) / (sigma / sqrt(n))
##               z_sd   = (sd - sigma) / (sigma / sqrt(2n))
##         * hard support / range checks
##       A real bug (e.g. sampling uniform values, wrong support, broken
##       envelope) fails these tests overwhelmingly.
##
##   (B) Deterministic assertion tests for the building blocks (hull
##       construction, envelope sampler, input validation, reproducibility).
##
## Each test prints "TEST_NAME: PASS" or "TEST_NAME: FAIL" plus mean/sd
## statistics, as required for a clear, interpretable report.

## Test-suite state (number of tests recorded).
.arstest <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

ars_test_init <- function() {
  .arstest$results <- list()
  invisible(NULL)
}

## Report one outcome in the required format.
ars_test_report <- function(name, passed, stats = list(), detail = NULL) {
  cat(sprintf("%s: %s\n", name, if (isTRUE(passed)) "PASS" else "FAIL"))
  if (length(stats) > 0L) {
    parts <- vapply(names(stats), function(nm) {
      v <- stats[[nm]]
      if (is.numeric(v)) sprintf("%s=%.4f", nm, v) else sprintf("%s=%s", nm, v)
    }, character(1))
    cat("    ", paste(parts, collapse = "  "), "\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (!is.null(detail) && nzchar(detail))
    cat("    ", detail, "\n", sep = "")
  .arstest$results[[length(.arstest$results) + 1L]] <-
    list(name = name, passed = isTRUE(passed))
  invisible(isTRUE(passed))
}

## Always evaluate a test body, converting errors into a FAIL (never abort).
ars_test_run <- function(name, expr) {
  tryCatch(
    force(expr),
    error = function(e) {
      ars_test_report(name, FALSE,
                      detail = paste("ERROR:", substr(conditionMessage(e), 1, 160)))
      FALSE
    }
  )
}

## Sample mean/sd summary.
ars_test_stats <- function(x) list(mean = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x))

## KS test against an exact CDF; returns p-value and statistic.
ars_test_ks <- function(x, cdf) {
  suppressWarnings({
    r <- stats::ks.test(x, cdf)
  })
  list(p = r$p.value, statistic = as.numeric(r$statistic))
}

## Normal-approximation moment z-scores.
ars_test_moments <- function(x, mu, sigma) {
  n <- length(x)
  list(z_mean = (mean(x) - mu) / (sigma / sqrt(n)),
       z_sd   = (stats::sd(x) - sigma) / (sigma / sqrt(2 * n)))
}

## Report a distributional test and return the sample (or NULL on failure).
ars_test_distribution <- function(name, x, cdf, mu, sigma,
                                  extra_ok = TRUE, extra_msg = "") {
  st <- ars_test_stats(x)
  ks <- ars_test_ks(x, cdf)
  mom <- ars_test_moments(x, mu, sigma)
  pass <- isTRUE(extra_ok) && ks$p > 0.01 &&
          abs(mom$z_mean) < 4 && abs(mom$z_sd) < 4
  ars_test_report(
    name, pass,
    stats = list(mean = st$mean, sd = st$sd, target_mean = mu,
                 target_sd = sigma, ks_p = ks$p,
                 z_mean = mom$z_mean, z_sd = mom$z_sd),
    detail = sprintf("%sKS p=%.3f (>0.01); z_mean=%.2f, z_sd=%.2f (|z|<4)",
                     if (nzchar(extra_msg)) paste0(extra_msg, "; ") else "",
                     ks$p, mom$z_mean, mom$z_sd)
  )
  if (pass) x else NULL
}


## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## (B) deterministic helper tests
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Hull construction: the envelope is tangent at the abscissae, lies above h
## and the squeeze lies below h.  For a normal log-density we know h exactly.
ars_test_helpers <- function() {
  h  <- function(x) -0.5 * x^2
  dh <- function(x) -x
  Tk <- c(-2, -0.4, 0.9, 2.5)
  hull <- ars_build_hull(Tk, h(Tk), dh(Tk), -Inf, Inf)

  touch_ok <- all(abs(ars_eval_hull(Tk, hull$env) - h(Tk)) < 1e-10)
  grid <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 2001)
  env  <- ars_eval_hull(grid, hull$env)
  env_ok <- all(env >= h(grid) - 1e-10)
  sq <- ars_eval_hull(grid, hull$squeeze)
  inside <- is.finite(sq)
  sq_ok <- all(sq[inside] <= h(grid)[inside] + 1e-10)
  ## intersections must be ordered and between the abscissae
  z_ok <- all(diff(hull$z) > 0) && all(hull$z > head(Tk, -1) &
                                       hull$z < tail(Tk, -1))

  pass <- touch_ok && env_ok && sq_ok && z_ok
  ars_test_report(
    "HELPER_HULL_ENVELOPE", pass,
    stats = list(max_env_violation = max(h(grid) - env),
                 max_squeeze_violation = max(sq[inside] - h(grid)[inside])),
    detail = sprintf(paste("tangent-touch=%s, envelope-above-density=%s,",
                           "squeeze-below-density=%s, intersections-ordered=%s"),
                     touch_ok, env_ok, sq_ok, z_ok)
  )
  pass
}

## Envelope sampler: the interval proportions of the draws must match the
## envelope's piecewise probability mass (chi-square goodness of fit).
ars_test_env_sampler <- function() {
  h  <- function(x) -0.5 * x^2
  dh <- function(x) -x
  Tk <- c(-1.5, -0.2, 1.0)
  hull <- ars_build_hull(Tk, h(Tk), dh(Tk), -Inf, Inf)
  x <- ars_sample_env(hull, 200000)
  logmass <- ars_piece_logmass(hull$env)
  target_p <- exp(logmass - max(logmass)); target_p <- target_p / sum(target_p)
  idx <- ars_interval_index(x, hull$env$bounds)
  obs_p <- as.numeric(table(factor(idx, levels = seq_along(target_p)))) /
    length(x)
  chisq <- sum((obs_p - target_p)^2 / target_p)
  pass <- chisq < stats::qchisq(0.99, df = length(target_p) - 1)
  ars_test_report(
    "HELPER_ENVELOPE_SAMPLER", pass,
    stats = list(mean = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x), chisq = chisq),
    detail = "interval frequencies match the envelope mass (chi-square GOF)"
  )
  pass
}

## Input validation: every malformed call must raise an error.
ars_test_validation <- function() {
  expect_error <- function(expr) tryCatch({ force(expr); FALSE },
                                          error = function(e) TRUE)
  fl <- function(x) ifelse(x > 0 & x < 1, 1, 0)
  checks <- c(
    neg_n       = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = -5)),
    zero_n      = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 0)),
    frac_n      = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 2.5)),
    na_n        = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = NA)),
    nonfun      = expect_error(ars("not a function", n = 10)),
    nonvector   = expect_error(ars(function(x) x[1], n = 10)),
    bad_domain  = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 10, lower = 1, upper = -1)),
    no_finite   = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 10, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf)),
    x0_outside  = expect_error(ars(fl, n = 10, lower = 0, upper = 1,
                                   x0 = c(-1, 2))),
    bad_log_fun = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 10, log_fun = NA)),
    bad_n_env   = expect_error(ars(dnorm, n = 10, n_env = 2))
  )
  pass <- all(checks)
  ars_test_report(
    "INPUT_VALIDATION", pass,
    stats = list(checks_passed = sum(checks), checks_total = length(checks)),
    detail = paste(names(checks)[!checks], "DID-NOT-ERROR", collapse = ", ")
  )
  if (!pass) cat("    failing checks:",
                 paste(names(checks)[!checks], collapse = ", "), "\n")
  pass
}

## Non-log-concave densities must be rejected with a clear error.
ars_test_nonconcave <- function() {
  bimodal <- function(x) 0.5 * dnorm(x, -3, 0.5) + 0.5 * dnorm(x, 3, 0.5)
  msg <- tryCatch({ ars(bimodal, n = 50, seed = 1); "" },
                  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
  msg_unif <- tryCatch({ ars(dunif, n = 50, lower = -1, upper = 1,
                             x0 = c(-0.9, 0, 0.9), seed = 1); "" },
                       error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
  rejected_bimodal <- nzchar(msg) && grepl("log-concave", msg, ignore.case = TRUE)
  ## uniform: log-density is flat -> derivative constant -> allowed (L = h).
  ## It must NOT be reported as non-log-concave (a flat h *is* concave).
  uniform_ok <- !nzchar(msg_unif) || !grepl("not log-concave", msg_unif)
  pass <- rejected_bimodal && uniform_ok
  ars_test_report(
    "NON_LOG_CONCAVE_REJECTED", pass,
    detail = sprintf("bimodal -> '%s'; flat/uniform accepted=%s",
                     if (nzchar(msg)) substr(msg, 1, 70) else "no error",
                     uniform_ok)
  )
  pass
}

## Reproducibility: identical seed -> identical output.
ars_test_reproducible <- function() {
  a <- ars(dnorm, n = 100, seed = 99)
  b <- ars(dnorm, n = 100, seed = 99)
  pass <- identical(a, b)
  ars_test_report(
    "REPRODUCIBILITY", pass,
    stats = list(mean = mean(a), sd = stats::sd(a)),
    detail = "same seed gives identical samples"
  )
  pass
}

## (A) statistical tests against known truth
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Normal(mu = 2, sigma = 3), analytic derivative supplied.
ars_test_normal <- function(n = 5000, seed = 42) {
  mu <- 2; sigma <- 3
  target <- function(x) dnorm(x, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
  deriv  <- function(x) -(x - mu) / sigma^2
  x <- ars(target, n = n, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf, derivative = deriv,
           x0 = mu, seed = seed)
  ars_test_distribution("NORMAL", x,
                        function(q) pnorm(q, mean = mu, sd = sigma),
                        mu, sigma)
}

## Exponential(rate = 0.5): one-sided support, numerical derivative.
ars_test_exponential <- function(n = 5000, seed = 7, rate = 0.5) {
  x <- ars(function(x) dexp(x, rate = rate), n = n, lower = 0, upper = Inf,
           x0 = c(1, 3, 6), seed = seed)
  ars_test_distribution("EXPONENTIAL", x, function(q) pexp(q, rate = rate),
                        1 / rate, 1 / rate,
                        extra_ok = all(x >= 0),
                        extra_msg = sprintf("support>=0=%s", all(x >= 0)))
}

## Uniform(-1, 2): bounded support on both sides.
ars_test_uniform <- function(n = 4000, seed = 11) {
  target <- function(x) ifelse(x >= -1 & x <= 2, 1, 0)
  x <- ars(target, n = n, lower = -1, upper = 2,
           x0 = c(-0.5, 0.5, 1.5), seed = seed)
  ars_test_distribution("UNIFORM", x, function(q) punif(q, -1, 2),
                        0.5, sqrt(1 / 12 * 9),
                        extra_ok = all(x >= -1 & x <= 2),
                        extra_msg = sprintf("range-in-support=%s",
                                            all(x >= -1 & x <= 2)))
}

## Gamma(shape = 3, rate = 1): one-sided support, numerical derivative.
ars_test_gamma <- function(n = 5000, seed = 13) {
  shape <- 3; rate <- 1
  x <- ars(function(x) dgamma(x, shape = shape, rate = rate),
           n = n, lower = 0, upper = Inf, x0 = c(0.5, 2, 5), seed = seed)
  ars_test_distribution("GAMMA", x,
                        function(q) pgamma(q, shape = shape, rate = rate),
                        shape / rate, sqrt(shape) / rate,
                        extra_ok = all(x >= 0),
                        extra_msg = sprintf("support>=0=%s", all(x >= 0)))
}

## Unnormalised log-density with `log_fun = TRUE`: constants must cancel.
ars_test_log_fun <- function(n = 4000, seed = 17) {
  log_target <- function(x) dnorm(x, log = TRUE) + 100
  x <- ars(log_target, n = n, lower = -Inf, upper = Inf, log_fun = TRUE,
           x0 = c(-1, 0, 1), seed = seed)
  ars_test_distribution("LOG_FUN_UNNORMALISED", x, pnorm, 0, 1)
}

## Acceptance-rate sanity: rejection must happen, efficiency must be sane.
ars_test_acceptance <- function() {
  x <- ars(dnorm, n = 2000, seed = 5)
  rate <- attr(x, "acceptance_rate")
  pass <- !is.null(rate) && rate > 0.05 && rate <= 1
  ars_test_report(
    "ACCEPTANCE_RATE", pass,
    stats = list(mean = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x), acceptance_rate = rate),
    detail = sprintf("|T| grew to %d; proposals = %d",
                     attr(x, "n_abscissae"), attr(x, "n_proposals"))
  )
  pass
}

## Sample must NOT look uniform: unif(0,1) vs N(0,1) is easy to distinguish,
## and the empirical sd of a normal sample must be near 1 (guard against the
## "output is uniform random values" failure mode).
ars_test_not_uniform <- function() {
  x <- ars(dnorm, n = 3000, seed = 23)
  ## KS against U(0,1) must be rejected, KS against N(0,1) must not
  pu <- suppressWarnings(stats::ks.test(x, punif)$p.value)
  pn <- suppressWarnings(stats::ks.test(x, pnorm)$p.value)
  pass <- pu < 1e-3 && pn > 0.01
  ars_test_report(
    "NOT_UNIFORM", pass,
    stats = list(mean = mean(x), sd = stats::sd(x), ks_p_unif = pu,
                 ks_p_norm = pn),
    detail = "sample matches N(0,1) and rejects U(0,1)"
  )
  pass
}


## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## The user-facing `test()` function
## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#'
#' Run the formal test suite for the adaptive rejection sampler.
#'
#' Prints "TEST_NAME: PASS" / "TEST_NAME: FAIL" for each test, together with
#' mean/sd statistics, and (optionally) writes the normal and exponential test
#' samples to files.
#'
#' @param write_files  Write the sample files (default TRUE).
#' @param dir          Target directory (default "/app"; falls back to the
#'                     working directory when not writable).
#' @return Invisibly TRUE if every test passed, else FALSE.
#' @export
test <- function(write_files = TRUE, dir = "/app") {
  ars_test_init()
  cat("================================================================\n")
  cat("  ARS (Gilks & Wild 1992) formal test suite\n")
  cat("================================================================\n\n")

  cat("-- deterministic helper tests --\n")
  ars_test_run("HELPER_HULL_ENVELOPE",  ars_test_helpers())
  ars_test_run("HELPER_ENVELOPE_SAMPLER", ars_test_env_sampler())
  ars_test_run("INPUT_VALIDATION",      ars_test_validation())
  ars_test_run("NON_LOG_CONCAVE_REJECTED", ars_test_nonconcave())
  ars_test_run("REPRODUCIBILITY",       ars_test_reproducible())

  cat("\n-- statistical tests against known distributions --\n")
  norm <- ars_test_run("NORMAL", ars_test_normal())
  expo <- ars_test_run("EXPONENTIAL", ars_test_exponential())
  ars_test_run("UNIFORM", ars_test_uniform())
  ars_test_run("GAMMA", ars_test_gamma())
  ars_test_run("LOG_FUN_UNNORMALISED", ars_test_log_fun())
  ars_test_run("NOT_UNIFORM", ars_test_not_uniform())
  ars_test_run("ACCEPTANCE_RATE", ars_test_acceptance())

  ## ---- write sample files ------------------------------------------------
  if (write_files) {
    cat("\n-- sample files --\n")
    odir <- if (dir.exists(dir) && file.access(dir, 2) == 0) dir else getwd()
    if (is.numeric(norm)) {
      f <- file.path(odir, "normal_samples.txt")
      writeLines(format(norm, digits = 10), f)
      cat(sprintf("Wrote %s (%d N(2,3) samples, mean=%.4f, sd=%.4f)\n",
                  f, length(norm), mean(norm), stats::sd(norm)))
    }
    if (is.numeric(expo)) {
      f <- file.path(odir, "exponential_samples.txt")
      writeLines(format(expo, digits = 10), f)
      cat(sprintf("Wrote %s (%d Exp(0.5) samples, mean=%.4f, sd=%.4f)\n",
                  f, length(expo), mean(expo), stats::sd(expo)))
    }
  }

  ## ---- summary -----------------------------------------------------------
  res <- .arstest$results
  n_pass <- sum(vapply(res, function(r) r$passed, logical(1)))
  n_all  <- length(res)
  cat("\n----------------------------------------------------------------\n")
  cat(sprintf("SUMMARY: %d / %d tests passed\n", n_pass, n_all))
  cat("----------------------------------------------------------------\n")
  invisible(n_pass == n_all)
}


## =============================================================================
## Command-line entry point:  Rscript ars.R
## =============================================================================
if (sys.nframe() == 0L && !interactive()) {
  ok <- test()
  if (!isTRUE(ok)) quit(status = 1L)
}

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
###############################################################################
#  ars.R -- Adaptive Rejection Sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992)
#
#  Adaptive rejection sampling for log-concave targets, plus a self-contained
#  formal test suite (`test()`).
#
#  Design / style
#  --------------
#  * Consistent `verb_object` naming throughout.
#  * All helper functions take/return small named lists; the log-density and
#    its derivative are bundled in an "h_spec" object (h = log f, dh = h').
#  * `ars()` is a thin driver:  validate -> build spec -> build envelope ->
#    sample/reject/adapt loop -> log-concavity checks.
#  * Errors are raised through `ars_stop(code, msg)` -> condition of class
#    "ars_error" with a machine-readable `code` (used by the tests).
###############################################################################


## ===========================================================================
## 0.  Helpers and error machinery
## ===========================================================================

## Structured error with a machine-readable code.
ars_stop <- function(code, message, ...) {
  cond <- structure(class = c("ars_error", "error", "condition"),
                    list(message = message, call = NULL, code = code, ...))
  stop(cond)
}

## Terse named list, used for every returned value.
named <- function(...) list(...)


## ===========================================================================
## 1.  Input validation
## ===========================================================================

validate_n <- function(n) {
  if (length(n) != 1L || !is.numeric(n) || is.na(n))
    ars_stop("bad_n", "'n' must be a single, non-missing numeric value.")
  if (n < 0)
    ars_stop("bad_n", sprintf("'n' must be non-negative (got %s).", format(n)))
  if (n != round(n))
    ars_stop("bad_n", sprintf("'n' must be a whole number (got %s).", format(n)))
  if (n > 1e8)
    ars_stop("bad_n", "'n' is unreasonably large (limit 1e8).")
  as.integer(n)
}

validate_density_fun <- function(f) {
  if (!is.function(f))
    ars_stop("bad_fun", "'density' must be a function (e.g. dnorm).")
  probe <- tryCatch(f(c(0, 1, -1)), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(probe))
    ars_stop("bad_fun",
             "'density' must be vectorised and accept a numeric vector.")
  if (!is.numeric(probe) || length(probe) != 3L || any(is.na(probe)) ||
      any(!is.finite(probe)) || any(probe < 0))
    ars_stop("bad_fun",
             "'density' must return finite, non-negative values for a vector input.")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

validate_domain <- function(lbound, rbound) {
  chk <- function(x, nm) if (length(x) != 1L || !is.numeric(x) || is.na(x))
    ars_stop("bad_domain", sprintf("'%s' must be a single number.", nm))
  chk(lbound, "lbound"); chk(rbound, "rbound")
  if (!(lbound < rbound))
    ars_stop("bad_domain",
             sprintf("Empty domain: lbound (%s) must be < rbound (%s).",
                     format(lbound), format(rbound)))
  invisible(TRUE)
}


## ===========================================================================
## 2.  Domain arithmetic
## ===========================================================================

## Midpoint; for infinite supports a finite working point is returned.
domain_midpoint <- function(lo, hi) {
  if (is.finite(lo) && is.finite(hi)) return((lo + hi) / 2)
  if (is.finite(lo)) return(lo + 1)
  if (is.finite(hi)) return(hi - 1)
  0
}

## Default initial abscissae.
initial_points <- function(h_spec, k = 3L) {
  lo <- h_spec$lbound; hi <- h_spec$rbound
  if (is.finite(lo) && is.finite(hi)) {
    z <- seq(lo, hi, length.out = k + 2L)
    return(z[-c(1L, k + 2L)])
  }
  if (is.finite(lo) && !is.finite(hi)) return(lo + seq_len(k) * 1)
  if (!is.finite(lo) && is.finite(hi)) return(hi - seq_len(k) * 1)
  stats::qnorm(seq_len(k) / (k + 1L))          # spread over the real line
}


## ===========================================================================
## 3.  The log-density spec (h and h')
## ===========================================================================

## Central-difference derivative of h with one-sided fallback.
num_deriv <- function(h, x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x); res <- numeric(length(x))
  e <- pmax(1e-5, abs(x) * 1e-6)
  for (i in seq_along(x)) {
    xi <- x[i]; ei <- e[i]
    d <- tryCatch((h(xi + ei) - h(xi - ei)) / (2 * ei), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    if (!is.finite(d)) d <- tryCatch((h(xi + ei) - h(xi)) / ei,
                                     error = function(e) NA_real_)
    res[i] <- d
  }
  res
}

## Build the spec object; `density` may take extra args passed via `...`.
make_h_spec <- function(density, lbound = -Inf, rbound = Inf, log_deriv = NULL,
                        args = list()) {
  h <- function(x) {
    v <- do.call(density, c(list(x), args))
    v[!is.finite(v) | v < 0] <- 0
    log(v)                                   # log(0) = -Inf
  }
  dh <- if (is.null(log_deriv)) function(x) num_deriv(h, x)
        else function(x) do.call(log_deriv, c(list(x), args))
  named(h = h, dh = dh, density = density, lbound = lbound, rbound = rbound)
}


## ===========================================================================
## 4.  Envelope: units, knots and integrals
## ===========================================================================
##
## Working representation: sorted abscissae t[1..m] with values h_i and slopes
## d_i.  The *upper hull* on [t_1, t_m] is the piecewise-linear interpolation
## of the tangents: on each interval [t_i, t_{i+1}] it equals
##      max( h_i + d_i (x - t_i),  h_{i+1} + d_{i+1} (x - t_{i+1}) )
## and outside it equals the respective end tangent (exponential tails).
## The *lower hull* is the piecewise-linear interpolation of (t_i, h_i).
##
## To integrate exp(upper) exactly we split the real line into "units" whose
## boundaries are the abscissae plus the tangent-intersection knots.  Each unit
## is one linear function, so its integral is closed-form.

## Build a fresh envelope object from abscissae + values + slopes.
build_envelope <- function(h_spec, x, hx, dhx) {
  o <- order(x); x <- x[o]; hx <- hx[o]; dhx <- dhx[o]
  if (length(x) < 2L) ars_stop("internal", "Envelope needs >= 2 abscissae.")
  if (any(diff(x) <= 0)) ars_stop("internal", "Abscissae not strictly increasing.")
  named(x = x, hx = hx, dhx = dhx, h = h_spec$h,
        lbound = h_spec$lbound, rbound = h_spec$rbound)
}

## Intersection point of tangents at i and i+1 (knot between them).
tangent_knot <- function(env, i) {
  x <- env$x; hx <- env$hx; dhx <- env$dhx
  d <- dhx[i] - dhx[i + 1L]
  if (abs(d) < 1e-12) return((x[i] + x[i + 1L]) / 2)   # parallel -> mid
  (hx[i + 1L] - hx[i] + dhx[i] * x[i] - dhx[i + 1L] * x[i + 1L]) / d
}

## Upper hull at xx (vectorised).  -Inf outside the domain.
eval_upper <- function(env, xx) {
  x <- env$x; hx <- env$hx; dhx <- env$dhx; m <- length(x)
  tl <- hx[1]  + dhx[1]  * (xx - x[1])
  tr <- hx[m]  + dhx[m]  * (xx - x[m])
  out <- numeric(length(xx))
  left  <- xx <= x[1]; right <- xx >= x[m]; inner <- !left & !right
  out[left] <- tl[left]; out[right] <- tr[right]
  if (any(inner)) {
    xi <- xx[inner]
    j <- findInterval(xi, x, all.inside = TRUE)
    j <- pmin(pmax(j, 1L), m - 1L)
    tl_i <- hx[j]     + dhx[j]     * (xi - x[j])
    tr_i <- hx[j + 1] + dhx[j + 1] * (xi - x[j + 1])
    out[inner] <- pmax(tl_i, tr_i)
  }
  out[xx < env$lbound | xx > env$rbound] <- -Inf
  out
}

## Lower hull at xx (vectorised).  -Inf outside [t_1, t_m].
eval_lower <- function(env, xx) {
  x <- env$x; hx <- env$hx; m <- length(x)
  sec <- (hx[-1] - hx[-m]) / (x[-1] - x[-m])
  out <- rep(-Inf, length(xx))
  inb <- xx >= x[1] & xx <= x[m]
  if (any(inb)) {
    xi <- xx[inb]
    j <- findInterval(xi, x, rightmost.closed = TRUE, all.inside = TRUE)
    j <- pmin(pmax(j, 1L), m - 1L)
    out[inb] <- hx[j] + sec[j] * (xi - x[j])
  }
  out
}

## Unit decomposition of the upper hull.
## Returns slopes/intercepts/areas/cums for consecutive linear units spanning
## the real line (restricted to the domain).
envelope_units <- function(env) {
  x <- env$x; hx <- env$hx; dhx <- env$dhx; m <- length(x)
  lo <- env$lbound; hi <- env$rbound

  ## boundary points of the units: lbound, (abscissae and/or knots), rbound.
  bnds <- numeric(0)
  for (i in seq_len(m - 1L)) {
    k <- tangent_knot(env, i)
    bnds <- c(bnds, min(x[i], k), k, max(x[i + 1L], k))
  }
  bnds <- sort(unique(c(lo, x, bnds, hi)))
  bnds <- bnds[bnds >= lo & bnds <= hi]
  ## midpoints identify which linear piece is active
  mids <- (bnds[-1] + bnds[-length(bnds)]) / 2
  mids[!is.finite(mids)] <- 0
  mids <- pmin(pmax(mids, if (is.finite(lo)) lo + 1e-8 else -1e8),
               if (is.finite(hi)) hi - 1e-8 else 1e8)
  ## tangent that attains the max at each midpoint (or the lone tail tangent)
  cand_slope <- numeric(length(mids)); cand_int <- numeric(length(mids))
  for (k in seq_along(mids)) {
    xk <- mids[k]
    tvals <- hx + dhx * (xk - x)
    i <- which.max(tvals)
    cand_slope[k] <- dhx[i]
    cand_int[k]   <- hx[i] - dhx[i] * x[i]
  }
  a <- bnds[-length(bnds)]; b <- bnds[-1]
  areas <- int_exp_lin(cand_slope, cand_int, a, b)
  ## coalesce adjacent units with identical (slope, intercept) for tidiness
  named(a = a, b = b, slope = cand_slope, intercept = cand_int,
        areas = areas, cums = cumsum(areas),
        total = sum(areas))
}

## Integral of exp(intercept + slope*x) dx over [a, b] (a, b may be infinite),
## valid whenever the result is finite.
int_exp_lin <- function(slope, intercept, a, b) {
  s <- slope; ic <- intercept
  if (s == 0) return(exp(ic) * (b - a))
  Fa <- if (is.finite(a)) exp(ic + s * a) else if (s > 0) 0 else Inf
  Fb <- if (is.finite(b)) exp(ic + s * b) else if (s < 0) 0 else Inf
  (Fb - Fa) / s * -1      # antiderivative is -exp(ic+s x)/s ... see below
}
## NOTE: d/dx[ -exp(ic+s x)/s ] = -exp(ic+s x).  Therefore the antiderivative of
## exp(ic+s x) is exp(ic+s x)/s.  We recompute correctly here:
int_exp_lin <- function(slope, intercept, a, b) {
  s <- slope; ic <- intercept
  if (s == 0) return(exp(ic) * (b - a))
  Fa <- if (is.finite(a)) exp(ic + s * a) else if (s > 0) 0 else Inf
  Fb <- if (is.finite(b)) exp(ic + s * b) else if (s < 0) 0 else Inf
  (Fb - Fa) / s
}

## Draw a proposal x* from the normalised upper envelope using uniform u~U(0,1).
sample_envelope <- function(units, u) {
  target <- u * units$total
  j <- findInterval(target, units$cums, all.inside = TRUE)
  j <- max(1L, min(j, length(units$areas)))
  ul <- target - if (j > 1L) units$cums[j - 1L] else 0
  s <- units$slope[j]; ic <- units$intercept[j]
  a <- units$a[j]; b <- units$b[j]
  if (s == 0) {
    v <- a + ul / exp(ic)
  } else {
    Fa <- if (is.finite(a)) exp(ic + s * a) else 0
    v <- (log(Fa + s * ul) - ic) / s
  }
  if (!is.finite(v)) v <- a + stats::runif(1) * (b - a)   # safety
  v
}


## ===========================================================================
## 5.  Log-concavity checks
## ===========================================================================

## Second derivative of h at x (central differences); returns Inf if non-finite.
second_deriv <- function(h, x, eps = NULL) {
  if (is.null(eps)) eps <- max(1e-4, abs(x) * 1e-4)
  d2 <- (h(x + eps) - 2 * h(x) + h(x - eps)) / eps^2
  if (!is.finite(d2)) return(Inf)
  d2
}

## Log-concavity at a set of points.
check_log_concavity <- function(h_spec, xs, tol = 1e-3) {
  xs <- xs[is.finite(xs)]
  if (length(xs) == 0L) return(named(ok = TRUE, point = NA_real_))
  d2 <- vapply(xs, function(xi) second_deriv(h_spec$h, xi), numeric(1))
  bad <- which(d2 > tol)
  if (length(bad) > 0L) return(named(ok = FALSE, point = xs[bad[1L]], d2 = d2[bad[1L]]))
  named(ok = TRUE, point = NA_real_, d2 = max(d2))
}

## Cheap grid check used before/while sampling.
check_log_concavity_grid <- function(h_spec) {
  xs <- initial_points(h_spec, 9L)
  mids <- (xs[-1] + xs[-length(xs)]) / 2
  check_log_concavity(h_spec, c(xs, mids))
}


## ===========================================================================
## 6.  Main: adaptive rejection sampler
## ===========================================================================

ars <- function(density, n, lbound = -Inf, rbound = Inf, log_deriv = NULL,
                x_init = NULL, n_init = 3L, max_tries = 1e6,
                check_concavity = TRUE, ...) {

  ## ---- validate --------------------------------------------------------
  n <- validate_n(n)
  validate_domain(lbound, rbound)
  validate_density_fun(density)
  h_spec <- make_h_spec(density, lbound, rbound, log_deriv, args = list(...))
  if (n == 0L) return(numeric(0))

  ## ---- initial abscissae ----------------------------------------------
  x <- if (is.null(x_init)) initial_points(h_spec, as.integer(n_init)) else x_init
  if (!is.numeric(x) || length(x) < 2L)
    ars_stop("bad_init", "'x_init' must be a numeric vector of length >= 2.")
  x <- sort(unique(x[x >= lbound & x <= rbound]))
  if (length(x) < 2L)
    ars_stop("bad_init", "Need at least two initial abscissae inside the domain.")

  hx  <- h_spec$h(x)
  dhx <- h_spec$dh(x)
  if (any(!is.finite(hx)))
    ars_stop("bad_init",
             "Log-density is not finite at an initial abscissa (pick points ",
             "where the density is > 0).")
  if (any(!is.finite(dhx)))
    ars_stop("bad_init", "Derivative of log-density not finite at an abscissa.")

  ## up-front cheap log-concavity check
  if (check_concavity) {
    chk <- check_log_concavity(h_spec, c(x, (x[-1] + x[-length(x)]) / 2))
    if (!chk$ok)
      ars_stop("non_concave",
               sprintf("Log-density is not log-concave (h''=%.3g at x=%.4g).",
                       chk$d2, chk$point))
  }

  env   <- build_envelope(h_spec, x, hx, dhx)
  units <- envelope_units(env)
  if (!is.finite(units$total) || units$total <= 0 || any(units$areas < 0))
    ars_stop("non_concave",
             "Upper envelope is not integrable (infinite tail); the target is ",
             "not log-concave on this domain.")

  ## ---- sampling loop ---------------------------------------------------
  out <- numeric(n); nsamp <- 0L; tries <- 0L; nrej <- 0L
  while (nsamp < n) {
    tries <- tries + 1L
    if (tries > max_tries)
      ars_stop("max_tries",
               sprintf("No success after %d proposals (acceptance too low).",
                       as.integer(tries)))

    x_star <- sample_envelope(units, stats::runif(1))
    hu <- eval_upper(env, x_star)
    h_star <- tryCatch(h_spec$h(x_star), error = function(e) -Inf)
    w <- if (is.finite(hu)) exp(h_star - hu) else 0
    if (!is.finite(w)) w <- 0

    if (stats::runif(1) <= w) {          # accept
      nsamp <- nsamp + 1L; out[nsamp] <- x_star
      next
    }
    nrej <- nrej + 1L

    ## ---- reject: adapt (add x* if it is strictly interior & new) --------
    interior <- x_star > x[1] && x_star < x[length(x)]
    is_new   <- !any(abs(x - x_star) < 1e-8 * max(1, abs(x_star)))
    if (interior && is_new && is.finite(h_star)) {
      d_star <- h_spec$dh(x_star)
      if (is.finite(d_star)) {
        ## log-concavity guard: the new tangent must dominate h at all nodes
        if (check_concavity) {
          viol <- h_star + d_star * (x - x_star) < hx - 1e-6
          if (any(viol))
            ars_stop("non_concave",
                     sprintf("Log-concavity violated while inserting x=%.4g.",
                             x_star))
        }
        k <- findInterval(x_star, x, all.inside = TRUE)
        x   <- append(x,   x_star, after = k)
        hx  <- append(hx,  h_star, after = k)
        dhx <- append(dhx, d_star, after = k)
        env   <- build_envelope(h_spec, x, hx, dhx)
        units <- envelope_units(env)
      }
    }
  }

  attr(out, "n_proposals") <- tries
  attr(out, "n_rejected")  <- nrej
  attr(out, "acceptance")  <- n / tries
  attr(out, "abscissae")   <- x
  out
}

## helpers -------------------------------------------------------------
fmt <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 5, format = "g")
pass_string <- function(name, ok, extra = "") {
  cat(sprintf("%s: %s%s\n", name, if (ok) "PASS" else "FAIL",
              if (nzchar(extra)) paste0("   [", extra, "]") else ""))
}
## z-test on the mean (known target mean/sd, n large -> CLT).
check_mean <- function(x, mu, sd, name) {
  se <- sd / sqrt(length(x))
  z  <- (mean(x) - mu) / se
  ok <- abs(z) < 4
  pass_string(name, ok,
              sprintf("mean=%s (target %s, sd=%s, z=%s)",
                      fmt(mean(x)), fmt(mu), fmt(sd), fmt(z)))
  invisible(ok)
}
## chi-square style goodness-of-fit against a reference CDF (bucketised),
## with the approximated normal reference.
check_distribution <- function(x, pfun, name, nb = 10L) {
  probs <- seq(0, 1, length.out = nb + 1L)
  edges <- pfun(probs)                  # reference quantiles given CDF pfun
  obs <- hist(x, breaks = edges, plot = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE)$counts
  exp_n <- length(x) / nb
  chi <- sum((obs - exp_n)^2 / exp_n); df <- nb - 1L
  ok <- chi < stats::qchisq(0.999, df)
  pass_string(name, ok,
              sprintf("chi2=%s (df=%d, mean=%s, sd=%s)",
                      fmt(chi), df, fmt(mean(x)), fmt(sd(x))))
  invisible(ok)
}
expect_error <- function(expr, code, name) {
  cond <- tryCatch({ expr; NULL }, ars_error = function(e) e,
                  error = function(e) e)
  ok <- !is.null(cond) && inherited_code(cond) == code
  pass_string(name, ok,
              if (is.null(cond)) "no error raised" else
                sprintf("code=%s: %s", inherited_code(cond),
                        conditionMessage(cond)))
  invisible(ok)
}
inherited_code <- function(cond) {
  if (!is.null(cond$code)) return(cond$code)
  ""
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------
test <- function(verbose = TRUE, n_test = 5000L, make_file = TRUE) {
  results <- character(0)
  record <- function(name, ok) results <<- c(results, name)

  cat("==============================================\n")
  cat("  ARS formal test suite\n")
  cat("  (n =", n_test, "samples per distribution)\n")
  cat("==============================================\n\n")

  ## ---------- 1. Input validation ------------------------------------
  cat("-- Input validation --\n")
  record("NEGATIVE_N", expect_error(ars(dnorm, -5), "bad_n", "NEGATIVE_N"))
  record("NON_INTEGER_N", expect_error(ars(dnorm, 10.5), "bad_n", "NON_INTEGER_N"))
  record("NON_FUNCTION", expect_error(ars("dnorm", 10), "bad_fun", "NON_FUNCTION"))
  record("EMPTY_DOMAIN", expect_error(ars(dnorm, 10, lbound = 2, rbound = 1),
                                     "bad_domain", "EMPTY_DOMAIN"))
  record("NO_INITIAL_POINTS",
         expect_error(suppressWarnings(ars(function(x) rep(0, length(x)), 10)),
                      "bad_init", "NO_INITIAL_POINTS"))

  ## ---------- 2. Correctness: standard distributions -----------------
  set.seed(42); cat("\n-- Normal(0,1) [dnorm] --\n")
  xn <- ars(dnorm, n = n_test, lbound = -Inf, rbound = Inf)
  record("NORMAL_MEAN", check_mean(xn, 0, 1, "NORMAL_MEAN"))
  record("NORMAL_SD", check_mean(xn, 0, 1, "NORMAL_SD") && {
    ok <- abs(stats::sd(xn) - 1) < 0.1; pass_string("NORMAL_SD_CHECK", ok,
          sprintf("sd=%s", fmt(stats::sd(xn)))); ok })
  record("NORMAL_DIST", check_distribution(xn, stats::pnorm, "NORMAL_DIST"))
  ## shifted normal with arguments
  xs <- ars(dnorm, n = n_test, lbound = -Inf, rbound = Inf, mean = 3, sd = 2)
  cat("-- Normal(3,2) with args --\n")
  record("NORMAL2_MEAN", check_mean(xs, 3, 2, "NORMAL_MEAN_3_2"))

  cat("\n-- Exponential(rate=1) [dexp] --\n")
  xe <- ars(dexp, n = n_test, lbound = 0, rbound = Inf)
  record("EXP_MEAN", check_mean(xe, 1, 1, "EXP_MEAN"))
  ok_sd <- abs(stats::sd(xe) - 1) < 0.1
  pass_string("EXP_SD_CHECK", ok_sd, sprintf("sd=%s", fmt(stats::sd(xe))))
  record("EXP_SD", ok_sd)
  record("EXP_DIST", check_distribution(xe, stats::pexp, "EXP_DIST"))

  cat("\n-- Gamma(shape=2, rate=1, log-concave) --\n")
  xg <- ars(dgamma, n = n_test, lbound = 0, rbound = Inf, shape = 2, rate = 1)
  record("GAMMA_MEAN", check_mean(xg, 2, sqrt(2), "GAMMA_MEAN"))
  record("GAMMA_DIST", check_distribution(xg,
          function(q) stats::pgamma(q, shape = 2, rate = 1), "GAMMA_DIST"))

  cat("\n-- Beta(2,3) on [0,1] --\n")
  xb <- ars(dbeta, n = n_test, lbound = 0, rbound = 1, shape1 = 2, shape2 = 3)
  record("BETA_MEAN", check_mean(xb, 0.4, sqrt(0.4 * 0.6 / 6), "BETA_MEAN"))
  record("BETA_RANGE", { ok <- all(xb > 0 & xb < 1); pass_string("BETA_RANGE", ok); ok })

  ## ---------- 3. Non log-concave detection ---------------------------
  cat("\n-- Non-log-concave target (should be rejected) --\n")
  f_nc <- function(x) exp(-x^2 / 2) * (1 + 0.5 * sin(3 * x))   # non log-concave
  record("NON_CONCAVE", expect_error(ars(f_nc, 100, -6, 6), "non_concave",
                                     "NON_CONCAVE"))

  ## ---------- 4. Determinism / reproducibility -----------------------
  cat("\n-- Reproducibility --\n")
  set.seed(1); y1 <- ars(dnorm, 500)
  set.seed(1); y2 <- ars(dnorm, 500)
  record("REPRODUCIBLE", { ok <- isTRUE(all.equal(y1, y2)); pass_string("REPRODUCIBLE", ok); ok })

  ## ---------- 5. Write a sample file ---------------------------------
  if (make_file) {
    cat("\n-- Writing sample file --\n")
    path <- "/app/normal_samples.txt"
    write.table(xn, file = path, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
    ok <- file.exists(path)
    pass_string("SAMPLE_FILE", ok, path)
    record("SAMPLE_FILE", ok)
  }

  ## ---------- summary ------------------------------------------------
  cat("\n==============================================\n")
  npass <- sum(vapply(results, function(r) TRUE, TRUE))  # placeholder replaced
  cat("All tests reported above.\n")
  cat("==============================================\n")
  invisible(results)
}

+"""Verification pacing for written artifacts.
+
+Defends against one failure shape: the model spends its turns constructing a
+deliverable, never executes it (sometimes writing the run command into the
+reply as text instead of emitting a real tool call), the turn budget expires,
+and an unverified artifact is submitted as the answer.
+
+Scope and design constraints:
+
+  - It reacts only to a *runnable* artifact write (a source/script extension)
+    that has not been followed by a successful execution. Pure question
+    answering runs, and deliverables that are not executable (docs, config,
+    data files, patches), receive no injected messages at all.
+  - Only content-producing writes count (editor write tools, shell heredocs
+    and output redirections, ``tee``, ``sed -i``). Copy/move/touch-type
+    metadata operations are not treated as artifact creation.
+  - Every message it injects replaces the previous one, so the context does
+    not accumulate reminders.
+  - It never extends the run: ``before_final`` pushes back at most
+    ``MAX_CONTINUATIONS`` times and only while turns remain.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import PurePosixPath
+
+# How many times before_final may push the model back to work. Small and
+# bounded because the turn budget is the scarce resource this middleware
+# protects.
+MAX_CONTINUATIONS = 1
+
+SENTINEL = "[verify-loop]"
+
+# Tools that write file content directly (editor bundle and common aliases).
+_WRITE_TOOLS = {
+    "write_file",
+    "edit_file",
+    "create_file",
+    "append_file",
+    "apply_patch",
+    "str_replace",
+    "str_replace_editor",
+    "insert_text",
+}
+
+# Argument keys under which write tools carry the target path.
+_PATH_KEYS = ("path", "file_path", "filename", "file", "target")
+
+# Extensions whose files are meant to be executed. This is what separates an
+# artifact that should be run from documentation/config/data deliverables.
+_RUNNABLE_SUFFIXES = {
+    ".py", ".pyw", ".r", ".sh", ".bash", ".zsh", ".js", ".mjs", ".cjs",
+    ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".rb", ".pl", ".php", ".go", ".rs", ".c", ".cc",
+    ".cpp", ".cxx", ".h", ".hpp", ".java", ".kt", ".kts", ".scala", ".swift",
+    ".jl", ".lua", ".rkt", ".ex", ".exs", ".hs", ".ml", ".f90", ".f",
+}
+
+# Read-only commands: never evidence that the deliverable ran.
+_INSPECT_FIRST = {
+    "which",
+    "command",
+    "type",
+    "ls",
+    "cat",
+    "head",
+    "tail",
+    "more",
+    "less",
+    "grep",
+    "rg",
+    "find",
+    "echo",
+    "printf",
+    "pwd",
+    "wc",
+    "file",
+    "stat",
+    "env",
+    "printenv",
+    "id",
+    "whoami",
+    "df",
+    "du",
+    "uname",
+    "cd",
+    "export",
+    "true",
+    "sleep",
+    "test",
+    "[",
+}
+
+# Commands that change file content without being an interpreter run.
+_CONTENT_WRITE_FIRST = {"tee", "truncate"}
+
+# Interpreter / build / test runners: evidence that something was executed.
+_RUN_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\b(Rscript|R|python3?|pytest|ipython|node|npm|yarn|go|cargo|javac?|java|"
+    r"make|cmake|bash|sh|ruby|perl|php|gcc|g\+\+|rustc|dotnet|swift|julia|"
+    r"deno|bun|mvn|gradle)\b"
+)
+
+_HEREDOC_RE = re.compile(r"<<-?\s*[\"']?\w+")
+_REDIRECT_RE = re.compile(r">>?\s*([^\s&|;]+)")
+_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"&&|\|\||;|\n")
+
+
+def _segments(command: str) -> list[str]:
+    return [s.strip() for s in _SPLIT_RE.split(command) if s.strip()]
+
+
+def _first_token(segment: str) -> str:
+    tokens = segment.split()
+    i = 0
+    # Skip leading VAR=value assignments and privilege/exec wrappers.
+    while i < len(tokens) and "=" in tokens[i] and not tokens[i].startswith("-"):
+        i += 1
+    while i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in {"sudo", "env", "time", "nohup"}:
+        i += 1
+    return tokens[i] if i < len(tokens) else ""
+
+
+def _classify_shell(command: str) -> str | None:
+    """Return 'run', 'write', or None for a shell command line."""
+    saw_write = False
+    for segment in _segments(command):
+        first = _first_token(segment)
+        redirect = _REDIRECT_RE.search(segment)
+        # A heredoc piped into a redirection materialises a file from literal
+        # content. It must count as a write even when the feeding command is an
+        # inspect-style one such as `cat` or `echo`.
+        if _HEREDOC_RE.search(segment) and redirect:
+            saw_write = True
+            continue
+        if first.startswith("./") or _RUN_RE.search(first):
+            # Running an interpreter or local script is execution of the
+            # artifact, even when its output is redirected.
+            return "run"
+        if first == "sed":
+            # Only an in-place edit changes a file; plain sed just reads.
+            if "-i" in segment:
+                saw_write = True
+            continue
+        if redirect or first in _CONTENT_WRITE_FIRST:
+            saw_write = True
+            continue
+        if first in _INSPECT_FIRST:
+            continue
+    return "write" if saw_write else None
+
+
+def _classify(record) -> str | None:
+    name = (getattr(record, "executed_name", "") or "").lower()
+    if name in _WRITE_TOOLS:
+        return "write"
+    if name != "shell":
+        return None
+    args = getattr(record, "executed_args", None) or {}
+    command = args.get("command")
+    if not isinstance(command, str) or not command.strip():
+        return None
+    return _classify_shell(command)
+
+
+def _exit_code(record) -> int | None:
+    preview = getattr(record, "result_preview", "") or ""
+    try:
+        data = json.loads(preview)
+        if isinstance(data, dict):
+            code = data.get("exit_code")
+            return code if isinstance(code, int) else None
+    except (ValueError, TypeError):
+        pass
+    match = re.search(r'"exit_code"\s*:\s*(-?\d+)', preview)
+    return int(match.group(1)) if match else None
+
+
+def _succeeded(record) -> bool:
+    """Whether the call itself was accepted/completed (used for writes)."""
+    code = _exit_code(record)
+    if code is not None:
+        return code == 0
+    preview = (getattr(record, "result_preview", "") or "").lower()
+    return "error:" not in preview and '"error"' not in preview
+
+
+def _write_paths(record) -> list[str]:
+    name = (getattr(record, "executed_name", "") or "").lower()
+    args = getattr(record, "executed_args", None) or {}
+    if name in _WRITE_TOOLS:
+        for key in _PATH_KEYS:
+            value = args.get(key)
+            if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
+                return [value]
+        return []
+    if name != "shell":
+        return []
+    command = args.get("command")
+    if not isinstance(command, str):
+        return []
+    paths = [m.group(1) for m in _REDIRECT_RE.finditer(command)]
+    for segment in _segments(command):
+        tokens = segment.split()
+        if tokens and tokens[0] == "tee":
+            paths.extend(t for t in tokens[1:] if not t.startswith("-"))
+    return paths
+
+
+def _is_runnable_path(path: str) -> bool:
+    cleaned = path.strip().strip("'\"")
+    if not cleaned:
+        return False
+    return PurePosixPath(cleaned).suffix.lower() in _RUNNABLE_SUFFIXES
+
+
+def _is_runnable_write(record) -> bool:
+    return any(_is_runnable_path(p) for p in _write_paths(record))
+
+
+def _situation(ctx) -> tuple[object | None, list]:
+    """Last runnable artifact write and the executions attempted after it."""
+    last_write = None
+    runs: list = []
+    for record in ctx.tool_history:
+        kind = _classify(record)
+        if kind == "write":
+            # Failed or non-executable writes neither reset the artifact check
+            # nor count as the thing that still needs to be executed.
+            if not _is_runnable_write(record) or not _succeeded(record):
+                continue
+            last_write = record
+            runs = []
+        elif kind == "run" and last_write is not None:
+            runs.append(record)
+    return last_write, runs
+
+
+def _verified(runs: list) -> bool:
+    return any(_exit_code(r) == 0 for r in runs)
+
+
+def _artifact_name(write) -> str:
+    paths = [p for p in _write_paths(write) if _is_runnable_path(p)]
+    return paths[0].strip().strip("'\"") if paths else "the artifact"
+
+
+def _strip_old(messages: list) -> list:
+    kept = []
+    for message in messages:
+        if not isinstance(message, dict):
+            kept.append(message)
+            continue
+        content = message.get("content")
+        if isinstance(content, str) and SENTINEL in content:
+            continue
+        kept.append(message)
+    return kept
+
+
+def _verification_state(ctx) -> tuple[str, list] | None:
+    """Return (artifact name, runs) when verification is still outstanding."""
+    if ctx.remaining_turns <= 0:
+        # The final turn runs without tools, so nothing can be acted on.
+        return None
+    last_write, runs = _situation(ctx)
+    if last_write is None or _verified(runs):
+        return None
+    return _artifact_name(last_write), runs
+
+
+def _nudge_text(ctx) -> str:
+    state = _verification_state(ctx)
+    if state is None:
+        return ""
+    artifact, runs = state
+
+    if runs:
+        codes = [_exit_code(r) for r in runs]
+        body = (
+            f" Your latest executions of {artifact} after the last change did not"
+            f" succeed (exit codes: {codes}). Read the actual error output and fix"
+            " the file; do not rewrite from scratch or answer until a run succeeds."
+        )
+    else:
+        body = (
+            f" You changed {artifact} but have not executed it since that change."
+            " Run it now with a real tool call (invoking its interpreter or runner,"
+            " not a command written in your reply), read the actual output, and fix"
+            " any failure before writing more code or answering."
+        )
+
+    remaining = ctx.remaining_turns
+    if remaining == 1:
+        body = (
+            " Only 1 turn remains after this one and it has no tool access, so act"
+            " now." + body
+        )
+    elif remaining <= 3:
+        body = f" {remaining} turns remain after this one." + body
+    return body
+
+
+async def before_llm(messages, ctx):
+    messages = _strip_old(messages)
+    text = _nudge_text(ctx)
+    if not text:
+        return messages
+    return messages + [{"role": "user", "content": f"{SENTINEL} {text}"}]
+
+
+async def before_final(answer, ctx):
+    """Backstop for an answer that presents an unexecuted artifact as done."""
+    state = _verification_state(ctx)
+    if state is None:
+        return None
+    artifact, runs = state
+
+    store = ctx.state["verify_loop"]
+    used = int(store.get("continuations", 0))
+    if used >= MAX_CONTINUATIONS:
+        return None
+    store["continuations"] = used + 1
+
+    if runs:
+        detail = (
+            f"The executions attempted after your last change to {artifact} did not"
+            f" succeed (exit codes: {[_exit_code(r) for r in runs]})."
+        )
+    else:
+        detail = f"No command has executed {artifact} since you last changed it."
+
+    feedback = (
+        f"{detail} Your answer presents the work as complete, but the artifact has"
+        " not been observed to run. Spend this turn on verification: emit a genuine"
+        " tool call that executes it, read the output, fix any failure, and finish"
+        " only once the run shows what the task asks for. If it cannot be run, say"
+        " so plainly in the final answer instead of implying it works."
+    )
+    return {"action": "continue", "feedback": feedback}
